fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a audience record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The audience's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable audience name shown in pickers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the audience — who they are and what they care about.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing the audience archetype and how to address them.

fields.name: seniority
fields.description: Typical seniority level of the audience. Engines use this as a hint for default depth and pacing.

fields.name: technicalFluency
fields.description: Typical technical fluency of the audience. AI generation uses this to decide whether to expand or assume technical terminology.

fields.name: decisionPower
fields.description: Whether the audience is expected to be informed, to advise, or to actually decide. Shapes the strength of the closing ask.

fields.name: attentionBudgetMinutes
fields.description: Realistic upper bound on this audience's focused attention for a single presentation, in minutes. Used as a hint when comparing against duration and the resolved narrative's duration range.

fields.name: recommendedNarratives
fields.description: Soft cross-link: ids of narratives in the same catalog that work well for this audience. Used by picker UIs to suggest narratives once an audience is chosen. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: recommendedTones
fields.description: Soft cross-link: ids of tones in the same catalog that work well for this audience. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Main preview image (PNG/JPG).

fields.name: thumbnailSrc
fields.description: Smaller thumbnail preview suited to dense grid views.

fields.name: vectorSrc
fields.description: SVG / vector preview for crisp scaling at any size.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Catalog kind, as the URL segment of the default catalog (`https://www.pptx.gallery/<kind>`) and the `packages/gallery/catalog/<kind>` directory name.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Index format version, as a string.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable description of what this catalog kind holds and how entries are ordered.

fields.name: contentSha256
fields.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical JSON of the full records this index lists, in index order, with every top-level `x-*` member removed. Canonical JSON sorts object keys and has no insignificant whitespace. Lets a consumer prove it holds exactly the published content.

fields.name: records
fields.description: Ordered list of lightweight record summaries. Order defines the catalog's canonical/display order; full record data lives in the sibling JSON file named by `file`.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier, matching the `id` field inside the record file named by `file`. Lowercase kebab-case; chart-type ids may start with a digit (e.g. '100pct-stacked-bar').

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable name shown in pickers.

fields.name: file
fields.description: Filename of the full record, relative to this index file's directory.

fields.name: deprecated
fields.description: Present on the entry of a record that carries `deprecation`. Pickers and default listings hide deprecated entries; the id keeps resolving.

fields.name: replacedBy
fields.description: The deprecated record's `deprecation.replacedBy`, repeated so a picker can offer the replacement without loading the record.

fields.name: publisher
fields.description: Base URL of the default-catalog publisher. Each kind is published at `<publisher>/<kind>/index.json`.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The published catalog files the snapshot was taken from.

fields.name: kinds
fields.description: One entry per catalog kind, keyed by the kind's URL segment.

fields.name: repository
fields.description: Git repository of the publisher.

fields.name: commit

fields.name: path

fields.description: Always 'mirror': the snapshot holds every record the publisher serves for the kind (OPF 0.15).

fields.name: records

fields.name: gallery
fields.description: The published catalog for this kind at the pinned commit.

fields.description: Human-readable name of the chart type, as a chart picker shows it.

fields.name: series
fields.description: Number of data series this chart type expects: exactly that many, except that a stacked or percent-stacked type and a combination (composition 'mixed', such as combo) expect at least that many. The editor offers a type that expects more than one series only for data with a fitting number of value columns; a one-series type fits one value column, and column, bar, line, area and radar types fit any number.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a font scheme record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The font scheme's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable scheme name shown in pickers.

fields.name: major
fields.description: Heading (major) font family — mirrors the OOXML majorFont entry.

fields.name: minor
fields.description: Body (minor) font family — mirrors the OOXML minorFont entry.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Optional monospaced font family name for code blocks and for inline code runs (TextRun.code). It has the same shape as the OPF FontScheme 'code' role, so a record and an inline design.fontScheme override are interchangeable. OOXML has no code slot, so exporters write this family on code runs. When neither design.fontScheme nor the resolved record defines 'code', engines fall back to Roboto Mono.

fields.name: eastAsian
fields.description: East Asian script fonts. Maps to the OOXML a:ea element of majorFont (major) and minorFont (minor), and to run-level a:ea. When set, they fill the eastAsian slot for every language; when omitted, the slot comes from this scheme's own major/minor when languageFamily is 'ea' and the scheme's languages list is empty or names the presentation language, then from the presentation language's font scheme for East Asian languages, and otherwise from the latin (major/minor) families. A missing 'major' or 'minor' falls back to the other.

fields.name: complexScript
fields.description: Complex-script fonts (for example Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and Thai). Maps to the OOXML a:cs element of majorFont (major) and minorFont (minor), and to run-level a:cs. When set, they fill the complexScript slot for every language; when omitted, the slot comes from this scheme's own major/minor when languageFamily is 'cs' and the scheme's languages list is empty or names the presentation language, then from the presentation language's font scheme for complex-script languages, and otherwise from the latin (major/minor) families. A missing 'major' or 'minor' falls back to the other.

fields.name: type
fields.description: High-level typographic class of the scheme.

fields.name: app
fields.description: Target application this font pairing is intended for. Metadata for pickers and catalog filters: no engine changes its output by it.

fields.name: languageFamily
fields.description: Font-language family this scheme is intended for: 'latin' for Latin-script content, 'ea' (or 'eastAsian', the same value) for East Asian scripts, 'cs' (or 'complexScript', the same value) for Complex Scripts. The long names match the 'eastAsian' and 'complexScript' slot keys; the short names match the OOXML a:ea and a:cs elements; core reads both spellings as one value. As the design font scheme, an 'ea'/'eastAsian' or 'cs'/'complexScript' scheme also fills that script slot with its own major/minor families when its languages list is empty or names the presentation language.

fields.name: languages
fields.description: Optional list of BCP-47 language tags this scheme is curated for. Useful for picker UIs that group fonts by language coverage. As the design font scheme, an 'ea' or 'cs' scheme fills its script slot only when this list is empty or names the presentation language: an entry matches a tag with the same language subtag (and the same script, when the entry names one).

fields.description: Short specimen string used by picker UIs to preview the scheme.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies this record as a language in the openpresentation.org catalog.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The record's id in the gallery's language catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Documents name a language by its BCP-47 tag ('bcp47'), never by this id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable language name.

fields.name: code
fields.description: ISO 639-3 (or 639-2) three-letter language code. Carried for engines that prefer ISO codes.

fields.name: bcp47
fields.description: BCP-47 language tag for this record. Use 'en-GB' for UK English; 'en-UK' is not a valid BCP-47 region form.

fields.name: ooxmlLang
fields.description: Curated culture tag for OOXML text-run language attributes (a:rPr/@lang, a:endParaRPr/@lang), in the language-[Script-]REGION form Office recognizes (e.g. 'ja-JP', 'ar-SA', 'ms-MY', 'nb-NO', 'fil-PH', 'zh-CN'). Engines emit it instead of 'bcp47' for a tag without a region; a region-bearing tag written by the author is emitted as written. Display metadata here: engines take the curated tag from their language vocabulary. Curated rather than inferred so output does not depend on the runtime's locale data.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Base text direction for the language. When omitted, engines derive it from the script: Arabic (Arab), Hebrew (Hebr), Syriac (Syrc), Thaana (Thaa), N'Ko (Nkoo), Adlam (Adlm), Samaritan (Samr), Mandaic (Mand) and Hanifi Rohingya (Rohg) are right-to-left; every other script is left-to-right. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows.

fields.name: script
fields.description: ISO 15924 script code of the language's writing system. The script selects the OOXML font slot the language's text uses: East Asian scripts (Hans, Hant, Hani, Jpan, Kore, Hang, Hira, Kana, Bopo, Yiii) use the eastAsian slot; complex scripts (for example Arab, Hebr, Syrc, Thaa, Deva, Beng, Guru, Gujr, Orya, Taml, Telu, Knda, Mlym, Sinh, Thai, Laoo, Tibt, Mymr, Khmr, Mong) use the complexScript slot; every other script (Latn, Cyrl, Grek, Armn, Geor, Ethi, ...) uses the latin slot. When omitted, engines infer it from the BCP-47 tag. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows. See docs/programs/font-fidelity-everywhere/script-font-model.md.

fields.description: The font-scheme id a picker suggests for this language when targeting PowerPoint output. Display metadata: engines take a language's default script fonts from their own vocabulary.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a layout template. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The layout's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field. 'auto' is reserved: Slide.layout 'auto' is automatic composition, so no catalog may define a layout of that id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable layout name, shown in layout pickers and as the PowerPoint layout name.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the layout — when to reach for it.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing the layout structure and ideal use cases.

fields.name: design
fields.description: The layout's design defaults, with the same keys and values as the deck's design and a slide's design (a slide overrides exactly what its layout sets, by the same name). An absent key means the layout has no opinion. Per key the slide's design wins, then the deck's design, then the resolved theme's design, then this record's design, then the engine default; 'variant' alone ranks this record above the deck and the theme (see DesignHints.variant). Composition, the renderer and the PPTX exporter all read the one result.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: How the record's 'regions' are laid out: 'row' places them side by side from the start edge in reading order (left to right; right to left in a right-to-left deck); 'column' stacks them top to bottom. Default 'column'.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Vertical position of the content of every body region when it is shorter than the region. A split's 'anchor' replaces it for the regions under that split, and a region's own 'anchor' replaces both. Only 'anchor' is inherited, and only by body regions: the heading regions 'title' and 'subtitle' never take it (they set their own, HeadingRegion.anchor), and the other region rules stay per region. One exception places the whole slide: when the record is a column and every entry of its 'regions' list is sized 'auto' (heading regions included), the record has no numeric row to hold the leftover height, so its 'anchor' places the whole stack, title and subtitle included, in the content box's leftover height: 'middle' centres it, 'bottom' sits it at the foot, 'top' (default) starts it at the top as before. A record with any numeric entry, a row record and an anchor on a split keep the rule above. Default 'top'.

fields.name: regions
fields.description: The record's regions in reading order: 1 to 12 entries, each a region ({ name, size?, ...rules }) or a split ({ direction, regions, size?, anchor? }). Every region is declared once, here, with its content rules; a block can target a body region with 'region': '<name>'. Names are unique across the whole record. 'size' is a number above 0 and up to 100 (default 1) that siblings share in proportion, separated by the gap; 'auto' is the height the content needs, allowed only in a column. 'title' and 'subtitle' are heading regions that take only a size (default auto in a column, 1 in a row), an anchor and (the 'title') a rule: 'title' holds the slide's heading group (tag, title and subtitle, stacked) and a 'subtitle' region takes the subtitle out of it, and a 'subtitle' needs a 'title'. A record with no 'title' region gets an implicit auto row on top for a slide that has headings. Splits nest at most three levels (the record's own list is level 1). Rules the schema cannot express (a reserved or repeated name, a 'subtitle' without a 'title', 'auto' outside a column, nesting too deep, more than 12 rows or columns once compiled) are the validate findings opf/layout-template and opf/layout-region.

fields.name: overflowRegion
fields.description: The region where content that no region accepts goes, whatever its 'accepts', while it has room; content beyond every region's room is drawn there too, with the warning opf/layout-unplaced. Omitted: the first primary region (in reading order) whose flow is not 'none'.

fields.description: 'title' or 'subtitle'.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Vertical position of the heading group in its area when the area is sized (a number): 'middle' (default) centers it, 'bottom' sets it at the foot of the area, as a cover or section sets its display title low, 'top' at the top. An 'auto' area is as tall as the group, so the anchor changes nothing there. A heading region never inherits the 'anchor' of the record or a split.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: 'title' only: draw a short accent rule (80 by 5 px at a 720 px short edge) half a gap above the title, at the title's start edge, on a slide with a title and no tag; a tag is the group's eyebrow and takes the rule's place. Engines draw it in the tag's color, the primary or the text color where the primary is under 4.5:1 on the slide. Default false.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: How the split's 'regions' are laid out: 'row' side by side, 'column' stacked.

fields.name: regions
fields.description: The split's regions in reading order: 1 to 12 regions and splits.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Vertical position of the content of every body region under this split, unless the region sets its own. The heading regions 'title' and 'subtitle' never inherit it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The region's name, lowercase kebab-case, unique across the whole record. A block targets it with 'region': '<name>'. It may not be 'title' (those are heading regions), 'tag', 'auto' or one of the promoted-region words ('start', 'center', 'end', 'top', 'middle', 'bottom'), so a Markdown block's region= option stays unambiguous: the validate finding opf/layout-region.

fields.name: accepts
fields.description: Content kinds the region takes: the body content kinds, and 'group' for a content group of any content. A region that takes 'image' also takes a shape block. A group is also accepted where every one of its leaf kinds is. Omitted: every body content kind and 'group'.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Which content the region wants first. Binding gives a picture (image, video) to a media region first, then primary, secondary, supporting; every other kind to a primary region first, then secondary, supporting, media; of two equal regions the first in reading order fills first. A supporting region receives content only when no primary or secondary region that accepts it has room, or by a pin. Default 'primary'.

fields.name: flow
fields.description: How several blocks share the region: 'none' one block fills it (blocks no region had room for join it, up to 6, and it flows as 'auto'); 'grid' by count (1 fills, 2 side by side, 3 in a row, 4 as 2 x 2, 5 as 3 + 2, 6 as 3 x 2, 7 to 12 in balanced rows of at most four, 9 as 3 x 3; rows and columns swap in a portrait region; the cells of a short row stretch to the full width, or keep one size and are centred in a grid of pictures); 'column' stacked at the heights the blocks need, one gap apart, and placed by the region's anchor (charts, pictures, tables, timelines and videos take what the measured blocks leave; blocks that do not fit share the region, each giving up the same fraction of what it can give up above its height at the minimum font size); 'auto' a grid when every block is short and a column when any block is long (more than 6 estimated lines in its grid cell at the starting size). design.contentDirection turns every flowing region into one row or one column. Default 'auto'.

fields.name: max
fields.description: Blocks the region holds on one slide. Default 1 for flow 'none' (which requires 1), else 6. Content beyond every region's room is drawn in the overflow region with the warning opf/layout-unplaced, and paginate moves it to a continuation slide.

fields.name: bleed
fields.description: The region's outer edges that lie on the content box's edge extend to the slide edge, as a placed image does. A bled region is never drawn as a card. Default false.

fields.name: listColumns
fields.description: 'auto': a list in the region that does not fit its cell at the starting size (a lone list, or one of several blocks) flows into up to three columns before it shrinks, as a list payload's columns: 'auto'; a list of 6 or fewer entries is never split. 2 or more lists alone in a region are one list per cell in a grid instead. Default 1.

fields.name: metrics
fields.description: How a metric block in the region is laid out. 'stack' (default): value, unit, label and the rest as one block at the region's anchor and content alignment. 'tile': the metric fills its cell (its card when the layout draws cards) from the start: the label first as an eyebrow, the value under it asking for a quarter of the cell's height (between its 76 px role size and twice it, fitted down as usual), and the description, delta and trend at the foot of the cell.

fields.name: sequence
fields.description: The region lists the steps of a sequence. 'steps': two or more text or list blocks are the steps, each under a numbered badge (an accent circle with its numeral; a one-entry numbered list gives the badge its number and draws as a heading over its description) on one connector line through the badge centers; a lone list's entries are the steps, each beside its badge on a connector down the badge column; a lone list of 3 to 6 entries of one or two words is a flow of chips joined by arrows. 'numbered' (an agenda, ordered by nature): every list of two or more entries of one level draws its entries beside badges, numbered or not; an unnumbered list is counted in arabic, continuing from the region's previous unnumbered list, as drawing only (the document keeps no numbering). Steps keep the text size they have without the badges: a slide whose blocks would get smaller draws them as before. Absent: the region's content draws as any other.

fields.name: arrangement
fields.description: The region draws its lone list as a diagram (docs/smartart.md), in the first design that holds every entry at one size, the list's role size or larger (up to 1.5 times), never smaller. PowerPoint's own geometry is tried first, which the PPTX export writes as live SmartArt where PowerPoint lays it out as the preview draws it; else OPF's own design fills the region as editable shapes. 'pyramid' (Basic Pyramid): 1 to 8 entries as stacked levels, the first at the apex, or OPF's stepped pyramid with each entry beside its level. 'inverted-pyramid': the same levels widest first, the tip at the bottom, entries still in their authored top-to-bottom order; exported as editable shapes (no live SmartArt is qualified for it). 'matrix' (Basic Matrix): exactly four entries as the quadrants of a centered square over a diamond, or four quadrants filling the region; another count draws a grid of cards. 'cycle' (Basic Cycle): 1 to 8 entries as circles on a ring, the first at the top and the rest clockwise, with an arrow from each to the next, or rounded rectangles on a ring. 'chevrons' (Basic Chevron Process): 1 to 8 entries as a row of chevrons; 'flow' (Basic Process): a row of boxes with arrows between them; 'vertical-flow' (Vertical Process): a column of them. These take a list of one level: a list with nested entries, descriptions, icons or numbering, more than 8 levels or steps, or one no design holds, draws as a list. 'org-chart' and 'hierarchy' take a list whose entry levels form one tree (the first entry at level 0, children at their depth); a skipped depth or a second root keeps the authored list. 'venn' draws 1 to 7 flat sets. Nodes are filled in the primary color with a 1.5 pt outline in the background color (cards in the card neutral), and a cycle's arrows are the primary lightened 40%. opf/arrangement-adapted (info) reports every list or grid of cards drawn in place of the arrangement. Absent: the region's content draws as any other.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Vertical position of the region's content when it is shorter than the region. Replaces the 'anchor' of the record and of the splits around it. Default: the nearest of those that sets one, else 'top'. A picture shown whole (fit 'contain') and a video, whose 16:9 frame is the largest that fits the cell, sit at the anchor inside the cell.

fields.name: empty
fields.description: What the region does on a slide that gives it no content: 'collapse' (default) joins its cells to a neighbouring area that shares the full length of one of its edges and is not itself empty; 'keep' leaves the space.

fields.name: titleAlignment
fields.description: Horizontal alignment of the title heading area. Logical, as design.titleAlignment of a deck: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on.

fields.name: contentAlignment
fields.description: Horizontal alignment of the body regions. Logical, as design.contentAlignment of a deck: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on.

fields.name: contentBox
fields.description: Whether the body regions are drawn inside a visible card or surface.

fields.name: contentDirection
fields.description: Axis along which parallel body content is arranged: 'vertical' is a column, 'horizontal' a row. On a layout slide it turns every flowing region into one row or one column; the slide's own composition.mode, columns and weights rank above it.

fields.name: chartPrimary
fields.description: Where the primary chart sits relative to supporting content on automatic slides. Template layouts express this arrangement with their regions; chartPrimary does not override a template.

fields.name: imageFit
fields.description: Default fit of the slide's image blocks: 'cover' fills the frame and crops around focus, 'contain' shows the whole picture, 'stretch' scales it to the frame, 'auto' covers when the crop keeps at least 85% of the picture and contains otherwise.

fields.name: listBullet
fields.description: Marker style of lists: 'character' draws the glyph, 'image' draws the deck's icon logo as a picture bullet, 'none' draws no marker and no hanging indent (label-and-description lists).

fields.name: listStyle
fields.description: As design.listStyle of a deck: 'stack' or 'rows' (ruled rows) for the lists of slides using this layout.

fields.name: mirror
fields.description: Draw the layout mirrored: each row's cells and the column sizes reversed, so a 'beside' layout puts its picture, chart or table at the end. Logical: a right-to-left deck mirrors on top. Binding and reading order do not change.

fields.name: variant
fields.description: The color variant slides on this layout draw on: a background slot ('accent1', 'dark1', ...) or the ColorVariant object, as design.variant, or a value relative to the deck's own variant (LayoutVariantRole: 'surface', 'brand'), so the layout keeps the deck's tone. Unlike the other keys it outranks the deck's design and the theme: the slide's own design.variant or design.background wins, then this, then the deck's variant or background, then the theme's. It hides a background of the deck or theme (the slide is the variant's bg1), and without an accent order of its own it keeps the deck's.

fields.name: gap
fields.description: Space between cells as a fraction of the container short edge (canvas at slide root). Default 0.03333333333333333.

fields.name: padding
fields.description: Inset as a fraction of the container short edge. Default 0.08 on a slide, 0 inside a group.

fields.name: minFontSize
fields.description: Minimum readable text size in reference pixels at a 720-pixel canvas short edge. Default 16. Overflow is diagnosed when text cannot fit at this size.

fields.name: overflow
fields.description: warn returns diagnostics for content that does not fit; error rejects layout. Content is never silently removed. Default warn.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a narrative record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The narrative's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable template name, e.g. 'Problem → Solution'.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence description of when and why to use this narrative.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing the narrative arc and ideal use cases. Used by AI-driven generation to seed deck-level direction.

fields.name: audienceFit
fields.description: Audiences this narrative works well for, e.g. ['executive', 'investor', 'customer'].

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Typical talk length this narrative suits, as a range in minutes. A deck's own target is the root 'duration' (one number); core validate warns when that target lies outside this range, and when 'min' is greater than 'max'.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search, e.g. ['business', 'pitch', 'internal'].

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional; engines fall back gracefully when previews aren't available.

fields.name: beats
fields.description: Ordered list of beats that make up the narrative arc.

fields.name: min
fields.description: Shortest talk length, in minutes, this narrative suits.

fields.name: max
fields.description: Longest talk length, in minutes, this narrative suits.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Main preview image (PNG/JPG). Used as the primary visual in picker UIs and previews of the record.

fields.name: thumbnailSrc
fields.description: Smaller thumbnail preview suited to dense grid views.

fields.name: vectorSrc
fields.description: SVG / vector preview for crisp scaling at any size.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable slug used by Slide.beat to reference this beat. Lowercase kebab-case.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable beat name, e.g. 'The Problem'.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Curator-written prose that explains what this beat should accomplish.

fields.name: instructions
fields.description: Short author-facing instruction for the beat — typically one phrase. Complements 'description' with a concise directive.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Default content kind for the beat's slide: the same values as Slide.type. Helps engines and planners choose a layout when only the beat is known.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: Suggested layout id for the beat's slide, e.g. 'section-divider', 'title-slide', 'text-left'. Resolves the same way as Slide.layout — against catalogs.layouts and the default catalog at https://www.pptx.gallery/layouts.

fields.name: thoughtCues
fields.description: Optional speaker or thinking cues for the beat: questions the slide should answer. A planner or author turns them into the slide's notes; no engine copies them there on its own.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Optional OPF schema version. When omitted, validators and engines should assume the latest supported OPF schema.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Display name of the presentation for GUI/TUI lists, library/search indexing, OS-level metadata, and default export filenames. This is deck identity, not slide content. Use slides[].title and slides[].subtitle for text that should appear on presented slides. Also the built-in variable 'deck.name'.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free-form prose describing what this presentation is about. Used by agents and humans as a deck-level summary; complements purpose (the goal) and narrative (the structured storyline). Round-trips to OOXML 'docProps/core.xml' as '<dc:description>' (PowerPoint surfaces this as the 'Comments' field in File → Properties). Also the built-in variable 'deck.description'.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: Optional base filename for exports (without extension). The opf CLI (convert) and the editor strip a trailing .pptx, .pdf, .png, or .svg (case-insensitive) and append the target format's extension. When omitted, they slugify name; with no usable name the CLI uses the input file name and the editor uses 'presentation'. See /docs/opf for full validation rules.

fields.name: organization
fields.description: Organization associated with the presentation, usually the presenting company. Array form supports hosts, partners, clients, and sponsors. The primary organization (Organization.role 'primary', else the first item) supplies the cover and section logo, the 'socials' header/footer field and the 'organization.<field>' built-in variables; the others are available by id as 'organization.<id>.<field>' and are not drawn automatically.

fields.name: speaker
fields.description: Person presenting the deck. Array form supports panels and multi-speaker decks. The first speaker is the primary speaker: the built-in variables 'speaker.<field>' read it, 'speakers' lists every name, and 'speaker.<id>.<field>' addresses one by id. A speaker is drawn nowhere else.

fields.name: author
fields.description: Optional credit for the person who authored or contributed to the deck, distinct from speaker. Array form supports multiple contributors. Round-trips to OOXML 'docProps/core.xml' as '<dc:creator>' (semicolon-joined when multiple) and seeds '<cp:lastModifiedBy>' on first write; subsequent edits in PowerPoint overwrite '<cp:lastModifiedBy>' with the editing user. Also the built-in variable 'deck.author' (an array joined with ', ').

fields.name: audience
fields.description:
Intended audiences for the presentation. Accepts any of:
- A single string: an audiences reference ('executive', or 'acme:board' for a record of the catalogs.acme group), or free-form text ('Series B investors'). A string that is a bare id or 'name:id' is a reference; any other string is free text and is never looked up.
- A single inline Audience object, for custom audience metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-audience/v1.
- An array of strings and/or inline Audience objects, for more than one audience.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the audience.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description:
Primary goal of the presentation. Accepts either:
- A string: a purposes reference ('decide', or 'acme:fundraise' for a record of the catalogs.acme group), or a free-form goal ('Raise a Series B round of $30M'). A string that is a bare id or 'name:id' is a reference; any other string is free text and is never looked up.
- An inline Purpose object for custom purpose metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-purpose/v1.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the purpose.

fields.name: language
fields.description:
Language of the presentation content, an engine vocabulary: a BCP-47 language tag, validated directly with no catalog lookup. Accepts either:
- A BCP-47 tag ('en-US', 'en-GB', 'ja', 'zh-Hans', 'ar-SA').
- An inline Language object: a 'bcp47' tag plus overrides of what engines know about it (name, ooxmlLang, script, direction, the script font schemes).

Engines know the script, base direction, OOXML language tag and default script fonts of the tags in spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json; any other well-formed tag is accepted and its script is inferred from the tag. Language names and descriptions are catalog display metadata, not part of the document.

fields.name: tone
fields.description:
Desired tone for the presentation. Accepts either:
- A tones reference: a bare id ('formal') or 'name:id' for a record of a named catalogs group.
- An inline Tone object for custom tone metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-tone/v1.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the tone.

fields.name: takeaway
fields.description: Audience-facing takeaway the presentation should leave behind. Array form supports multiple takeaways. Deck-level intent used by AI to seed and pressure-test slide content.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Target presentation duration, as an integer number of minutes. The opf-render presenter view counts the elapsed time against it, and core validate warns when it lies outside the resolved narrative's 'duration' range. Agents can also use it to set pace and depth. Nothing else reads it: the preview and the PPTX export draw no duration.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels used for categorization, search, and filtering. Lowercase kebab-case is recommended for consistency across a deck library.

fields.name: design
fields.description: Optional design system covering theme, color scheme, font scheme, dimensions, background, logo, watermark, header, and footer applied to the deck. When omitted, engines use their default design configuration.

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Optional named variables: deck colors referenced as 'var:<id>' (the original use), and typed content variables (text, number, date, image, url, list) referenced inline as '{{<id>}}' or whole as 'var:<id>'. Variables are what makes a deck a fillable template when combined with 'template': true. Color variables complement the color scheme: scheme slots and roles stay the primary vocabulary; variables cover deck-specific named colors that have no scheme slot. Built-in variables ('{{speaker.name}}', 'var:organization.logo', 'deck.name', ...) need no declaration; see Variables.

fields.name: template
fields.description: Marks this document as a template: an incomplete OPF file. A template declares variables (top-level 'variables') and references them from content, and may leave required variables unfilled; validation then reports the unfilled variables instead of failing, and previews and exports use each variable's 'example'. Filling a template (resolveVariables, or 'opf fill') returns a normal deck with this marker removed. Absent or false: a normal deck, where an unfilled required variable is an error. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

fields.name: narrative
fields.description:
The deck's narrative plan, by reference: a bare narratives id ('classic-story') or 'name:id' for a record of a named catalogs group ('acme:founder-pitch'). The deck holds only this pointer; the plan (the arc, its beats and what each beat must do) lives in the record, which has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-narrative/v1. A narrative the document defines itself is a record in catalogs.custom.narratives, referenced here by its key.

Slides link themselves to beats with slides[].beat. Core validate warns about a slides[].beat id the resolved narrative does not define and about a root 'duration' outside its 'duration' range, and reports a beat that no slide references. The preview and the PPTX export draw nothing from the narrative; opf-pptx stores the reference for round-trip.

The reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference, never an error.

Deck-level concerns that are not part of the storyline (audience, tone, takeaway, duration) live as siblings on the presentation root.

fields.name: slides
fields.description: Ordered array of slides that make up the presentation.

fields.name: references
fields.description: Sources that text runs cite with 'cite'. Ids are unique. A cited reference is listed in the footnote area of every slide that cites it, with a marker number assigned per deck in order of first use; a reference no run cites is the warning opf/unused-reference. referencesSlide() turns the cited references into an ordinary list slide.

fields.name: datasets
fields.description: Optional shared data tables, keyed by id. A chart ('chart.data': { "dataset": "<id>" }) or a table ('table': { "dataset": "<id>" }) references one instead of holding its own copy; engines inline the reference before composing, rendering or exporting. A dataset nothing references is the warning opf/unused-dataset. See docs/chart-table-data.md.

fields.name: assets
fields.description: Optional reusable asset registry for images, data files, videos, documents, fonts, and other resources referenced elsewhere in the deck via 'asset:<id>' strings.

fields.name: icons
fields.description: Optional deck-local icons, keyed by name: an author's or an LLM's own SVG, written once and named by any `icon` of the deck. See docs/icons.md.

fields.name: catalogs
fields.description: The catalog records this document embeds, grouped by the catalog they came from: 'default' (the catalog bare ids come from), 'custom' (records the document defines itself) and any number of named catalogs ('acme', referenced as 'acme:<id>'). A saved document embeds every record it references, so it renders the same with no catalog registered. See Catalogs.

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Resource source. Accepts an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path resolved against the OPF file location, or local filesystem path.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Alternative text for images and other visual assets.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-readable asset title for editors and asset pickers.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional notes about the asset's contents, provenance, or intended use.

fields.name: mediaType
fields.description: Optional MIME media type when it cannot be inferred from src.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Image source. Accepts an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path resolved against the OPF file location, or local filesystem path.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Alternative text for the image.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-readable asset title for editors and asset pickers.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional notes about the asset's contents, provenance, or intended use.

fields.name: mediaType
fields.description: Optional MIME media type when it cannot be inferred from src.

fields.name: callouts
fields.description: Editable text panels over this image. Coordinates are fractions of its visible frame, measured from the physical top-left even in RTL. Panels are drawn above masks and overlays; overflowing text is reported, never clipped or shrunk below the body role.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Plain editable text. Native edits preserve current words; an empty string is retained.

fields.name: x
fields.description: Signed fraction of the visible image frame width from its physical left edge. A callout points at pixels, and a picture never mirrors, so this coordinate is physical in every language. Negative values or values greater than 1 position the panel outside the image; its text is not clipped to the image. The slide crops what lies outside it; a callout wholly outside the slide is the warning opf/shape-off-slide.

fields.name: y
fields.description: Signed fraction of the visible image frame height from its physical top edge. Negative values or values greater than 1 position the panel outside the image; its text is not clipped to the image. The slide crops what lies outside it.

fields.name: width
fields.description: Positive fraction of the visible image frame width, at most 1. The signed x origin controls placement outside the frame.

fields.name: height
fields.description: Positive fraction of the visible image frame height, at most 1. The signed y origin controls placement outside the frame.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional audiences reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved before applying the inline overrides.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable audience name shown in pickers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the audience.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing the audience and how to address them.

fields.name: seniority
fields.description: Typical seniority level of the audience.

fields.name: technicalFluency
fields.description: Typical technical fluency of the audience.

fields.name: decisionPower
fields.description: Whether the audience is expected to be informed, advise, or decide.

fields.name: attentionBudgetMinutes
fields.description: Realistic upper bound on focused attention for a single presentation, in minutes.

fields.name: recommendedNarratives
fields.description: Soft cross-link: narrative ids that work well for this audience, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: recommendedTones
fields.description: Soft cross-link: tone ids that work well for this audience, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional purposes reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved before applying the inline overrides.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable purpose name shown in pickers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the purpose.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing when to use this purpose and how it should shape a deck.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: Desired audience outcome after the presentation.

fields.name: successCriteria
fields.description: Observable signals that the deck accomplished this purpose.

fields.name: recommendedNarratives
fields.description: Soft cross-link: narrative ids that work well for this purpose, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: recommendedTones
fields.description: Soft cross-link: tone ids that work well for this purpose, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable language name.

fields.name: bcp47
fields.description: BCP-47 language tag used for locale-aware rendering, proofing, and accessibility metadata. Use 'en-GB' for UK English; 'en-UK' is not a valid BCP-47 region form.

fields.name: ooxmlLang
fields.description: Culture tag for OOXML text-run language attributes (a:rPr/@lang, a:endParaRPr/@lang), in the language-[Script-]REGION form Office recognizes (e.g. 'ja-JP', 'ar-SA', 'ms-MY', 'nb-NO', 'fil-PH', 'zh-CN'). Without it, engines emit the curated tag of their language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) for a tag without a region, and a region-bearing tag as written. Curated rather than inferred so output does not depend on the runtime's locale data.

fields.name: code
fields.description: ISO 639-3 or 639-2 language code carried for engines that prefer ISO codes.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Base text direction for the language. When omitted, engines derive it from the script: Arabic (Arab), Hebrew (Hebr), Syriac (Syrc), Thaana (Thaa), N'Ko (Nkoo), Adlam (Adlm), Samaritan (Samr), Mandaic (Mand) and Hanifi Rohingya (Rohg) are right-to-left; every other script is left-to-right. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows. A right-to-left deck mirrors its layout, and one rule says what follows it. Layout words and layout coordinates are logical: 'start' and 'end' in alignments, header and footer zones, promoted regions, image placement, overlay bands, chartPrimary and shape anchors, the order of side-by-side blocks and columns, and an overlay shape's 'x' all run from the edge the deck starts on. Coordinates and sides that name pixels of a picture or parts of a plot are physical in every language: ImageFocus, ImageCallout 'x', a chart's 'legend' and data label 'position', and the 'left' and 'right' of table cell borders and paddings and of a shape's padding.

fields.name: script
fields.description: ISO 15924 script code of the language's writing system. The script selects the OOXML font slot the language's text uses: East Asian scripts (Hans, Hant, Hani, Jpan, Kore, Hang, Hira, Kana, Bopo, Yiii) use the eastAsian slot; complex scripts (for example Arab, Hebr, Syrc, Thaa, Deva, Beng, Guru, Gujr, Orya, Taml, Telu, Knda, Mlym, Sinh, Thai, Laoo, Tibt, Mymr, Khmr, Mong) use the complexScript slot; every other script (Latn, Cyrl, Grek, Armn, Geor, Ethi, ...) uses the latin slot. When omitted, engines infer it from the BCP-47 tag. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows. See docs/programs/font-fidelity-everywhere/script-font-model.md.

fields.name: fontScheme
fields.description: Font-scheme reference (a bare id or 'name:id') for this language's script slot when targeting PowerPoint output. Its major/minor families fill the language's script slot (eastAsian or complexScript, chosen by 'script') unless the effective design font scheme sets that slot itself; the latin slot always follows the design font scheme. Without it, engines use the default script fonts of their language vocabulary.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier for the organization, used to reference it from Speaker.organizationId and to address it in built-in variables as 'organization.<id>.<field>'. Must be unique among organizations (a duplicate is a validation error).

fields.name: name

fields.name: logo

A path, URL or Asset is one logo for every shape; an object gives up to four shapes (full, stacked, icon, wordmark), each a path or Asset, or { onLight, onDark } for the two backgrounds. A path is resolved against the OPF file location; an HTTPS URL, data URI or 'asset:<id>' reference works too. SVG (preferred for vector logos) or PNG with transparency are typical. The primary organization's full logo (role 'primary', else the first organization) is drawn on cover and section slides unless design.logo names another or is false. Every logo is also a slide-scoped built-in image, placed with a whole-field reference in any image field: 'var:organization.logo' (the full logo), 'var:organization.logo.icon' (likewise stacked, wordmark, full), and 'var:organization.<id>.logo' or 'var:organization.<id>.logo.<shape>' for another organization. A missing shape falls back to full, and full to the first defined of wordmark, stacked and icon. The onLight or onDark value is chosen for each slide's background; a missing one uses the other. See docs/templates-and-variables.md and docs/design-resolution.md.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Role of the organization relative to the presentation. Only 'primary' has behavior: it selects the primary organization (cover and section logo, the 'socials' header/footer field, and the 'organization.<field>' built-ins). When no organization has role 'primary', the first one is primary. 'partner', 'client', 'sponsor' and 'host' are descriptive labels that change nothing.

fields.name: socials
fields.description: Optional social media handles or URLs for the organization. The primary organization's socials render in header/footer zones that set socials: true; otherwise they are authoring metadata.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier for the speaker. Must be unique among speakers (a duplicate is a validation error). Addresses this speaker in built-in variables as 'speaker.<id>.<field>', such as '{{speaker.alice.title}}'.

fields.name: name

fields.name: title
fields.description: Role or title. Built-in variable 'speaker.title' (or 'speaker.<id>.title'), for example in a footer text of '{{speaker.name}}, {{speaker.title}}'.

fields.name: photo
fields.description: Source for the speaker's headshot image. Accepts an HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path (resolved against the OPF file location), local path, or 'asset:<id>' reference. Common formats are JPG or PNG; SVG is not appropriate for photographic content. Never drawn automatically: it is the built-in image variable 'speaker.photo' (or 'speaker.<id>.photo'), placed with 'var:speaker.photo' in a slide's image field. It also round-trips through PPTX provenance.

fields.name: email
fields.description: Contact email. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'speaker.email'.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: Contact phone number for the speaker. E.164 format is recommended. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'speaker.phone'.

fields.name: bio

fields.name: organizationId

fields.name: socials
fields.description: Optional social media handles or URLs for the speaker. Authoring metadata only: nothing draws speaker socials and there is no built-in variable for them (the 'socials' header/footer field draws the primary organization's socials).

fields.name: theme
fields.description: Theme for the deck: a themes reference, a bare id ('minimal') or 'name:id' ('acme:brand'). The theme supplies the default colour scheme, font scheme, background and dimensions; design.colorScheme, design.fontScheme, design.background and design.dimensions override it field by field. A reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference and engines use the engine default theme.

fields.name: colorScheme
fields.description:
Color scheme for the presentation. Accepts two forms:
- A colorSchemes reference: a bare id ('cool-horizon') or 'name:id' ('acme:ocean').
- Object form: a ColorScheme with an optional 'id' reference as the base plus slot/role overrides. Without 'id', the overrides apply on top of the engine default colour scheme.

Without either, the theme's colorScheme applies, then the engine default colour scheme.

fields.name: fontScheme
fields.description:
Font scheme for heading, body, accent, and code text. Accepts two forms:
- A fontSchemes reference: a bare id ('aptos') or 'name:id' ('acme:inter').
- Object form: a FontScheme with an optional 'id' reference as the base plus pair/role overrides.

Without either, the theme's fontScheme applies, then the engine default font scheme.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.description: Slide dimensions and aspect ratio. String shorthand such as 'widescreen' is equivalent to { preset: 'widescreen' }.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Default slide background applied across the deck unless overridden on a slide (slides.N.design.background); the resolved theme's background is the fallback. A background is the only canvas fill and never moves content. String shorthand accepts theme slots ('light1', 'light2', 'dark1', 'dark2'), hex colors, or an image source starting with 'asset:', 'https://', 'data:', './' or '../' (a cover image); object forms support theme, solid, gradient, image, or pattern fills.

fields.name: variant
fields.description: Optional color variant, as a background slot ('light1', 'light2', 'dark1', 'dark2', or an accent 'accent1' to 'accent6'; the same as { background: slot }) or the object form, which is needed only for an accent order: which slot of the color scheme is the slide background (and so which are the text and the alternate surface), and optionally the order of the accents. A variant is a mapping over the same twelve-slot scheme, as PowerPoint's color map is, never a second scheme. Without it the background decides: a theme-slot background ('dark1', { type: 'theme', slot }) is the variant of that slot, a picture or gradient takes its 'tone', and any other background picks light or dark by its luminance. A slide's variant replaces the deck's whole, including its accent order. A slide's layout record can name a variant too (layout design.variant): it outranks the deck's and the theme's, and the slide's own variant or background still wins.

fields.name: logo
fields.description: Which logo covers, section dividers and picture bullets draw. Logos live on the organization (Organization.logo); without this field covers and sections draw the primary organization's full logo and picture bullets its icon. A logo reference overrides that: 'var:organization.beta.logo' draws organization beta's logo, and a reference that names a shape ('var:organization.logo.wordmark') draws that shape everywhere this field applies. false draws no logo. A slide's design.logo overrides the deck's; absence inherits. An override naming an organization without a logo draws nothing (validation warns). Placement (reference engines, vetoable): on a cover or section slide (no body payload on a heading-only layout such as title, title-subtitle or section-divider, or no layout) the logo is drawn at the top-left of the free area, inside the slide padding and below any header furniture, in a box 56 reference pixels tall and at most four times as wide; the tag/title/subtitle group then centers in the remaining span. Content slides never get an automatic logo; a header or footer zone places one with image: 'var:organization.logo.icon'. composeSlide returns the cover box as geometry.logo.

fields.name: watermark
fields.description: Optional decorative watermark applied across slides: an image or a text stamp, in the fixed frame and at the opacity described on Watermark. Use false to suppress an inherited watermark in slide-level design; a string or Asset is the image at opacity 0.08.

fields.name: header
fields.description: Repeated header furniture rendered outside the main slide content. Use false to suppress an inherited header.

fields.name: footer
fields.description: Repeated footer furniture rendered outside the main slide content. Use false to suppress an inherited footer.

fields.name: titleAlignment
fields.description: Default horizontal alignment for the title heading area (the title and the tag) in resolved layouts. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.titleAlignment, then the layout record's design.titleAlignment, then the engine default. Logical: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on (the left for left-to-right text, the right for right-to-left text) and 'end' is the opposite edge.

fields.name: contentAlignment
fields.description: Default horizontal alignment for body/content regions in resolved layouts. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentAlignment, then the layout record's design.contentAlignment, then the engine default. The tag follows titleAlignment (and so does a subtitle in the title area, as on a cover) unless the slide's own design sets contentAlignment. Logical: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on (the left for left-to-right text, the right for right-to-left text) and 'end' is the opposite edge.

fields.name: contentBox
fields.description: Whether body/content regions are rendered inside a visible card or surface. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentBox, then the layout record's design.contentBox, then the engine default.

fields.name: contentDirection
fields.description: Axis along which parallel body content is arranged: 'vertical' is a column, 'horizontal' a row. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentDirection, then the layout record's design.contentDirection. On a slide with a template layout it turns every flowing region of the slide into one row or one column, below the slide's own composition.mode, columns and weights, which arrange its first primary flowing region. On an automatic slide (and a 0.18 record) it sets the root arrangement mode when no composition.mode is set on the slide or on its layout record. Promoted regions (start, top:start, ...) keep their explicit geometry and nested groups keep their own composition.

fields.name: chartPrimary
fields.description: Where the primary chart sits relative to supporting content. Effective value: slide design, then deck design, then the layout record's design.chartPrimary. It applies to automatic slides only; a template layout says the same with its regions (chart-beside). When the slide has no promoted regions and no composition.mode of its own, and its root nodes mix at least one chart with other content, the first chart becomes a primary track and the other nodes form one synthetic sub-grid: 'start'/'end' is a two-track row with the chart on that side (logical: 'start' is the left in a left-to-right deck and the right in a right-to-left one) and 'top'/'bottom' a two-track column, weighted 3:2 in favor of the chart; explicit root columns and weights are ignored while it applies. 'none' (the default) keeps the ordinary automatic grid with equal weight. Automatic composition builds direct content groups; template regions remain authoritative.

fields.name: imageFit
fields.description: Default fit of image blocks (and Slide.image) that set no fit of their own: 'cover' fills the frame and crops what overflows around the block's focus, 'contain' shows the whole picture in a frame of its own proportions, centered across and placed down the cell by the region's anchor (top by default), 'stretch' scales it to the frame exactly, 'auto' covers when the crop keeps at least 85% of the picture's width or height (its proportions read from the file, EXIF orientation applied) and contains otherwise; an SVG, or a picture whose size cannot be read from the document, is contained. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.imageFit, then the layout record's design.imageFit, then 'cover'; a slide composed with no layout shows its pictures whole ('contain') instead. Backgrounds set their own fit.

fields.name: listBullet
fields.description: Marker style for items and bullets lists. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.listBullet, then the layout record's design.listBullet, then 'character'. 'character' (the default) draws the glyph marker. 'image' draws the primary organization's icon logo (or the organization and shape design.logo names; the onDark value on dark backgrounds) as a picture bullet: a square with side 0.65 times the marker's font size whose bottom sits on the marker baseline, so list geometry does not change. Without a logo the glyph is drawn and the engine reports unresolved-content at this field. 'none' draws no marker and no hanging indent, so each entry's text (and its description) starts at the left edge of the list: use it for label-and-description lists such as pillars, team members and questions with answers. Nested levels keep their indent. A list that sets numbering still draws its numbers.

fields.name: listStyle
fields.description: How list entries are arranged. 'stack' draws each entry's text with its description under it, the entries close together, as before. 'rows' draws ruled rows: a hairline between two first-level entries (the scheme's border neutral, 1 reference pixel), 0.8 em between rows and no bullet (a numbered list keeps its numbers); when every entry has a description and sits at the first level, the labels are bold and, when the widest fits 40% of the list's width on one line, sit in a column beside their descriptions, first baselines aligned, else each description sits under its label. Both engines draw the rules (PowerPoint: native lines). Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.listStyle, then the layout record's design.listStyle. Without one, a list of two or more first-level entries that each pair a short label (3 words or fewer, no full stop) with a description is drawn as rows when that sets no block of the slide smaller, and every other list is stacked.

fields.name: mirror
fields.description: Draw the slide's template layout mirrored: each row's cells and the column sizes reversed, so a 'beside' layout puts its picture, chart or table at the end. Logical: a right-to-left deck mirrors on top. Binding and reading order do not change. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the layout record's design.mirror, then false. Slides without a template layout ignore it.

fields.name: opacity

fields.name: tone

fields.name: type

fields.name: gradient
fields.description: Gradient fill definition: a linear gradient along 'angle' (default 0, left to right). A shape fill's Gradient also takes radial and path types; a background does not.

fields.name: opacity

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Gradient angle in degrees (0 = left-to-right, 90 = top-to-bottom).

fields.name: stops
fields.description: Ordered list of color stops along the gradient. A gradient needs at least two stops.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Stop color: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

fields.name: position
fields.description: Stop position along the gradient, from 0 (start) to 1 (end).

fields.name: tone
fields.description: Whether the background is dark or light, which picks the color map (dark1 or light1) so text, lines and neutrals read on it. Without a tone a picture or gradient takes the deck's variant, else counts as light.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Picture background.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Source for the background image: an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, or a relative path resolved against the OPF file location.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Alternative text. A background with alt is meaningful: PowerPoint export draws it as a full-slide picture at the back that carries the text, so screen readers see it. Without alt it is decorative and exports as the native slide background; the alt text of a referenced asset does not count, so a background is decorative unless it says otherwise.

fields.name: fit
fields.description: How the picture fills the canvas: 'cover' fills it and crops what overflows around focus; 'contain' shows the whole picture centered over the colour scheme's default background; 'stretch' scales it to the canvas exactly; 'tile' repeats it at its own size from the top-left corner. Default 'cover'.

fields.name: focus
fields.description: Point of the picture to keep in view when 'cover' crops it. Ignored by the other fits. Without a focus a portrait picture (taller than wide) cropped into a wider frame keeps y 0.3 so heads stay in frame; every other crop is centered.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Picture opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque); the overlay keeps its own opacity. Default 1.

fields.name: recolor
fields.description: Grayscale or duotone treatment of the picture's pixels, as on an image block: recolor and opacity apply to the pixels, then the overlay is drawn above.

fields.name: overlay
fields.description: Scrim over the whole picture or a band along one edge (edge, size), beneath furniture and content, for example to keep a title readable over a busy photo. Without an overlay, core draws an automatic scrim in the slide's background color behind text that sits on the picture, at the lowest opacity that keeps it at 4.5:1 over any picture (a gradient from the edge the text is near, or a band across it). An overlay of the author's replaces the automatic scrim, and false turns it off.

fields.name: textPlacement
fields.description: Where a cover's or section's heading group goes on this picture: the top, middle or bottom of its area, start-aligned or centered, or 'panel' (a start-side column on the background color; needs no overlay key). Absent: core picks the calmest place when the host measured the picture (SlideComposition.pictureText).

fields.name: x
fields.description: Horizontal position, 0 (left edge) to 1 (right edge).

fields.name: y
fields.description: Vertical position, 0 (top edge) to 1 (bottom edge).

fields.name: color
fields.description: Overlay fill color: a hex color (eight-digit hex keeps its alpha), a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Overlay fill opacity.

fields.name: edge
fields.description: Cover only a band along this edge of the frame, for example a caption strip. Backgrounds and rectangle image frames only; on another shape the overlay is not drawn and composition reports unsupported-image-treatment. Omit to cover the whole frame. 'start' and 'end' follow the deck's direction: the left and right sides in a left-to-right deck, the right and left sides in a right-to-left one.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Band share of the frame for an edge overlay. Default 0.3. Ignored without edge.

fields.name: edge
fields.description: The slide edge the image bleeds to.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Share of the slide width (start, end) or height (top, bottom) given to the band. Default 0.5.

fields.name: inset
fields.description: Draw the frame inside the slide padding on every side of the band, like a card, instead of edge to edge. Default false.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Line color: any ColorRef (eight-digit hex keeps its alpha). Default the shape style's line color, or the slide's neutral line on a picture.

fields.name: gradient
fields.description: A gradient line instead of a solid color (a:ln/a:gradFill).

fields.name: width
fields.description: Line width in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge. 0 removes the line. Default 4/3 (1 point, PowerPoint's default line) on a shape, 2 on a picture.

fields.name: dash
fields.description: Dash pattern: a preset name or an array of dash and gap lengths in stroke widths.

fields.name: cap
fields.description: Line cap (a:ln cap flat, rnd, sq). Default flat.

fields.name: join
fields.description: Line join (a:miter, a:round, a:bevel). Default miter, PowerPoint's default line join.

fields.name: miterLimit
fields.description: Miter join limit, as a multiple of the stroke width (a:miter lim). Default 8. Ignored by round and bevel joins.

fields.name: compound
fields.description: Compound line (a:ln cmpd sng, dbl, thickThin, thinThick, tri). Default single.

fields.name: align
fields.description: Where the line sits on the outline (a:ln algn ctr or in). Default center. PowerPoint draws inside-aligned lines only on closed outlines.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Arrowhead at the start of an open path (a:headEnd).

fields.name: end
fields.description: Arrowhead at the end of an open path (a:tailEnd).

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: Hand-drawn look (PowerPoint's Sketched line, ask:lineSketchStyleProps): curved, freehand or scribble. OPF computes the sketched outline from a seed and both engines draw it: the preview strokes it and the PPTX stores it, which PowerPoint draws as stored, so the two match. A stroked path's fill follows the sketched outline too. PowerPoint versions before 2021 draw the plain line.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Arrowhead kind, DrawingML's ST_LineEndType. Default 'triangle' when the object is given.

fields.name: width
fields.description: Arrowhead width relative to the stroke width (2, 3 or 5 stroke widths). Default medium.

fields.name: length
fields.description: Arrowhead length relative to the stroke width (2, 3 or 5 stroke widths). Default medium.

fields.name: type
fields.description: linear runs along 'angle'; radial spreads from the center as a circle, rectangle as a rectangle and shape along the shape's own outline (a:path circle, rect, shape). Default linear.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Linear gradients only: angle in degrees (0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom). Default 90.

fields.name: stops
fields.description: Ordered color stops; at least two. A radial, rectangle or shape gradient runs from the center (position 0) to the outline (position 1).

fields.name: color
fields.description: Stop color: any ColorRef (eight-digit hex keeps its alpha).

fields.name: position
fields.description: Stop position, 0 to 1.

fields.name: preset
fields.description: DrawingML pattern preset (ECMA-376 ST_PresetPatternVal), for example pct5, ltHorz, wdUpDiag, smGrid or dotDmnd.

fields.name: foregroundColor
fields.description: Pattern color. Default the shape style's fill color.

fields.name: backgroundColor
fields.description: Color behind the pattern. Default the slide background.

fields.name: d
fields.description: SVG path data in the viewBox.

fields.name: viewBox
fields.description: The path's own box, 'minX minY width height' as in SVG; it is stretched to the block.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Shadow color. Default black.

fields.name: size

fields.name: color

fields.name: opacity

fields.description: Opacity where the reflection starts.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: Gap between the shape and its reflection in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: blur
fields.description: Blur radius in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: dark
fields.description: Color at luminance 0.

fields.name: light
fields.description: Color at luminance 1.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Fixed pattern background fill.

fields.name: pattern
fields.description: Pattern fill definition.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Background opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

fields.name: preset
fields.description: Pattern preset or engine-defined pattern id. DrawingML preset names (ECMA-376 ST_PresetPatternVal, for example pct5, ltHorz, wdUpDiag) are portable: PPTX export writes them as native pattern fills and import returns the same name. Engine-defined ids are renderer-specific; the legacy preview id diagStripe remains accepted and exports as wdUpDiag.

fields.name: foregroundColor
fields.description: Foreground color for the pattern: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

fields.name: backgroundColor
fields.description: Background color behind the pattern: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

fields.name: full
fields.description: The full logo (lockup): mark and name side by side. Drawn on cover and section slides, and placed by 'var:organization.logo'.

fields.name: stacked
fields.description: The stacked lockup: mark above the name, for portrait or square slots. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.stacked'.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: The mark or symbol without the name, for tight spaces such as header and footer zones and picture bullets. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.icon'.

fields.name: wordmark
fields.description: The name set in the brand's lettering, without the mark. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.wordmark'.

fields.name: onLight
fields.description: The logo for light backgrounds, usually dark artwork.

fields.name: onDark
fields.description: The logo for dark backgrounds, usually light or white artwork.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Source for the watermark image: an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path or local path, as for Asset.src. Exactly one of src and text is set.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text for a text watermark, such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL; line breaks are drawn as spaces. Exactly one of src and text is set.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Watermark opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

fields.name: start
fields.description: Content at the start edge, aligned to it.

fields.name: center
fields.description: Centered header/footer content.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Content at the end edge, aligned to it.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text rendered in this zone. Variables resolve inside it like any string: deck-wide ones ('{{organization.name}}', '{{speaker.name}}, {{speaker.title}}', '{{customer}}') before composition, and the slide-scoped built-ins '{{slide.number}}', '{{slide.section}}' and '{{deck.slideCount}}' for each slide as it is laid out. Each '{{slide.number}}' is a live slide-number field: PPTX export writes it as a native field when its value fits within one accepted text line, and as static text with a diagnostic otherwise. '{{deck.slideCount}}' is fixed text, because PowerPoint has no slide-count field. Write '\{{' for literal braces.

fields.name: image
fields.description: Image rendered first in this zone's row, such as a logo, partner mark, certification badge, or icon: a path, URL or Asset, or an organization logo reference ('var:organization.logo.icon', 'var:organization.<id>.logo.wordmark'), which resolves for each slide's background (onLight or onDark).

fields.name: date
fields.description: true renders the current date: the renderer or exporter must be given an explicit ISO date by its host (core never reads a clock). PPTX export writes a native date field only for a supported dateFormat whose complete value fits within one accepted text line; otherwise it writes static text with a diagnostic. Native PowerPoint refresh and save/reopen compatibility require separate verification. A string is fixed: with dateFormat it must be an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date and is formatted; without dateFormat it is literal text rendered as written.

fields.name: dateFormat
fields.description: Date pattern for date. Tokens: yyyy (2026), yy (26), MMMM (April), MMM (Apr), MM (04), M (4), dd (09), d (9), EEEE (Thursday), EEE (Thu). Text in single quotes and other non-letter characters are literal. Month and weekday names are English, independent of host locale. Defaults to "M/d/yyyy" for a current date. PPTX export writes a native current-date field only when its complete value fits within one accepted text line and the pattern matches a PowerPoint en-US date field ('M/d/yyyy'; 'EEEE, MMMM d, yyyy'; 'd MMMM yyyy'; 'MMMM d, yyyy'; 'd-MMM-yy'; 'MMMM yy'; 'MMM-yy'). Other patterns and wrapped fields export as static text with a diagnostic. Full provenance can recover generated-date intent from unchanged supported wrapped dates on OPF reimport; the existing PPTX text remains static.

fields.name: socials
fields.description: Whether to render the primary organization's social profiles from organization.socials, one line per platform in key order. A handle is formatted through the platform's socialPlatforms record (companyUrlPattern, else profileUrlPattern, else baseUrl, with handlePrefix stripped) and shown as that profile URL without its 'https://' scheme; a value that is already a URL is shown without an 'https://' scheme; an unknown platform key shows the raw value. Exporters link each line to its full URL when one exists. Speaker socials are not rendered by this field.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional stable identifier, unique among slide, payload and overlay ids in the document. A connector names it in 'from' or 'to'.

fields.name: x
fields.description: The shape's start edge as a signed fraction of the slide width, measured from the slide's start edge: the left edge in a left-to-right deck, the right edge in a right-to-left one. A shape sits over the layout, and the layout mirrors, so this coordinate is logical; only the position mirrors, never the geometry (an arrow keeps the way it points). Negative values or values greater than 1 place the shape partly or wholly outside the slide; a shape wholly outside it is the warning opf/shape-off-slide. With 'y', 'width' and 'height'.

fields.name: y
fields.description: Top edge as a signed fraction of the slide height, from the top edge. Negative values or values greater than 1 place the shape partly or wholly outside the slide.

fields.name: width
