fields.description: Width as a fraction of the slide width, from 0 (a vertical line) to 8. Above 1 the shape is wider than the slide, for a circle or band that bleeds off it; the slide crops what lies outside.

fields.name: height
fields.description: Height as a fraction of the slide height, from 0 (a horizontal line) to 8. Above 1 the shape is taller than the slide.

fields.name: layer
fields.description: Overlay shapes only. front (the default) draws the shape over the slide: above the content and the furniture. back draws it behind the slide: above the background and the watermark, below the content and the furniture (a panel or band behind a block). Array order stacks the shapes within each layer. Connectors are always in front.

fields.name: connector
fields.description: Makes the entry a connector: what it joins and how it runs.

fields.name: shape
fields.description: The preset geometry, as on a shape block. Default rect.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Custom geometry instead of a preset (a:custGeom), as on a shape block.

fields.name: adjust
fields.description: The preset's adjust handles (a:avLst) in OPF units, as on a shape block. On a connector, the adjust values of its connector preset (adj1 of an elbow or a curve between sites on one axis, a fraction of the frame's width), which replace the automatic route's, so a route made in PowerPoint is kept exactly.

fields.name: fill
fields.description: 'none', a ColorRef, { gradient } or { pattern }. Default the style's fill.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: The fill's opacity (a:alpha). Default 1.

fields.name: stroke
fields.description: A shape's line along its outline (default the style's line), or a connector's line: color, width, dash, compound, sketch and arrowheads ('start' at 'from', 'end' at 'to'; default a 2-pixel line in the slide's text color with no arrowheads).

fields.name: style
fields.description: The theme shape style, as on a shape block. Default moderate.

fields.name: shadow
fields.description: Outer shadow.

fields.name: innerShadow
fields.description: Inner shadow.

fields.name: glow
fields.description: Glow.

fields.name: softEdge
fields.description: Soft edges (a:softEdge), radius in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: reflection
fields.description: Reflection.

fields.name: blur
fields.description: Blur of the whole shape (a:blur), radius in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: rotate
fields.description: Rotation in degrees, clockwise, about the shape's center (a:xfrm rot). Its connection sites turn with it.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Mirror the geometry (a:xfrm flipH, flipV). The text is not mirrored.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text inside the shape's text rectangle (a string or TextRun[]), fitted by OPF's measured fonts from the body size down to the readability floor and never below it.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Vertical placement of the text in the text rectangle (a:bodyPr anchor). Default middle.

fields.name: padding
fields.description: Text insets inside the text rectangle.

fields.name: textDirection
fields.description: Text direction (a:bodyPr vert). Default horizontal.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Alternative text (p:cNvPr descr). Without it the shape's text is what is read.

fields.name: decorative
fields.description: Mark the shape decorative (a16:decorative): screen readers skip it.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Keep the shape in the file but do not draw it (p:cNvPr hidden). A link on a hidden shape is a validation finding (opf/shape-link-hidden).

fields.name: link
fields.description: URL opened when the shape is clicked in a slide show (a:hlinkClick): an http(s) URL, a 'mailto:' address or a 'tel:' number.

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips.

fields.name: block
fields.description: The id of a block on this slide (a content payload or a group, at any depth).

fields.name: edge
fields.description: The edge of the block the shape sits outside of, or its center.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The gap between the block's edge and the shape, in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge; a negative offset overlaps the block. Default 0. Ignored for 'center'.

fields.name: width
fields.description: The shape's width as a fraction of its target's width: the block's box, or with 'point' the chart mark's bounds. 1 is the target's own width and 1.08 a frame 8% wider. For a size in pixels use 'widthPx'; not both. Default: the preset's natural proportions with the shape's shorter side at 15% of the target's shorter side (at least 12 reference pixels on a chart mark).

fields.name: height
fields.description: The shape's height as a fraction of its target's height. For a size in pixels use 'heightPx'; not both. Default as for width.

fields.name: widthPx
fields.description: The shape's width in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge, whatever size its target has: a badge or a ring of a fixed size. Instead of 'width'.

fields.name: heightPx
fields.description: The shape's height in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge. Instead of 'height'.

fields.name: point
fields.description: Exact unique category label or zero-based data row index of the chart. Numeric strings name labels; numbers index rows. Empty/duplicate labels can be selected by index. Requires a supported classic chart block.

fields.name: series
fields.description: Exact unique plotted value-column name or zero-based plotted-series index; omission selects the first plotted series. Requires point. Scatter X is not a value series.

fields.name: from
fields.description: The id of the block or overlay shape on this slide the connector starts at. An id that is not on the slide is a finding (opf/connector-end-missing) and the connector is not drawn.

fields.name: to
fields.description: The id of the block or overlay shape on this slide the connector ends at.

fields.name: route
fields.description: straight is one segment (straightConnector1); elbow runs horizontally and vertically (bentConnector3, bentConnector2 between perpendicular sites); curved is PowerPoint's curved connector (curvedConnector3, curvedConnector2 between perpendicular sites). Default straight.

fields.name: fromSite
fields.description: The connection site index at 'from' (DrawingML's cxn idx), instead of the automatic choice. An index the shape does not have is a validation error.

fields.name: toSite
fields.description: The connection site index at 'to', instead of the automatic choice.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional stable identifier for the slide within the document. Use when another system needs to reference a slide across edits, comments, generation state, exports, or narrative tooling. Slide order is defined by the slides array, so simple decks may omit this.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Language of this slide, overriding the presentation language. Accepts the same BCP-47 tag or inline Language object as the presentation. Omission inherits the deck language. Direction, script fonts, quotation marks, line breaking and number formatting follow the effective slide language; TextRun.lang still overrides an individual run.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Optional full-slide content kind. When omitted, engines infer the kind from root payload fields.

fields.name: beat
fields.description: Optional reference to one or more beats of the deck's narrative (each value is the id of a beat in the narrative record that the root 'narrative' resolves to). A single string declares the slide's primary beat; an array declares that one slide covers multiple beats. Declares the slide's role in the story arc; does not constrain ordering or structure. Core validate warns about a beat id the resolved narrative does not define, and reports a beat that no slide references. Slides without a beat are valid; multiple slides may share a beat.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: Optional layout: a layouts reference, a bare id ('pillars') or 'name:id' ('acme:hero'), or 'auto'. When omitted or 'auto', the slide is composed with no layout record: engines arrange title, subtitle, tag and content automatically, a slide with no body payload is a cover (vertically centered), and design hints apply; there is no finding. 'auto' is reserved, so no catalog may define a layout of that id, and opf format drops it. A layout is a grid template (layout.schema.json): the slide's content stays flat and binds to the layout's regions by reading order, role and kind, a block may pin itself to a region with 'region', and an empty region collapses. A reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference (and the 'unresolved-reference' diagnostic of resolveSlideContext), the slide composes automatically, and a strict export fails. A layout id of the 0.18 default catalog that 0.19 no longer has is such a reference: 0.19 has no migration path for layouts. A layout never changes what a slide contains, and engines never substitute a different layout.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Slide-level title content. A v2 layout renders this in its title heading area, or an implicit heading row when that area is absent. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.description: Slide-level subtitle or supporting line. A v2 layout renders this in its subtitle area when present, otherwise in the title heading group. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

fields.name: tag
fields.description: Small slide-level label or badge. A v2 layout renders this before the title in its title heading group; tag is not a separate layout area. Engines draw it as an eyebrow: 22 reference pixels, bold, in the primary color (the text color where that is under 4.5:1 on the background) and, where its script has case, in capitals with 0.08 em of letter spacing (PowerPoint: cap=all and spc on the authored text). Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Full-slide text payload. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Full-slide structured list payload. Presence of this field infers type 'list'. Entries are strings, TextRun[] or objects with `text`, optional `description` (supporting detail under the entry), `level` and `start`. Use `items` when entries share a shape (features, steps, options, risks) or any entry needs a `description`; use `bullets` for plain talking points. Both draw the same marker, nesting and numbering; they differ in the inferred kind and in `description`, which only `items` accepts. At slide root, multiple content payload kinds with no explicit type, blocks, or regions are accepted as shorthand for layout-agnostic blocks, so `items` next to `text` or `bullets` composes as separate blocks side by side.

fields.name: bullets
fields.description: Full-slide prose bullet payload: short talking points, each standing alone. Presence of this field infers type 'text', so it may sit beside `text` in one payload. Entries are strings, TextRun[] or objects with `text`, `level` and `start`; there is no `description` (use `items` for entries with supporting detail).

fields.name: numbering
fields.description: Number the full-slide `items` or `bullets` instead of bulleting them. A style name (arabic, roman-upper, roman-lower, alpha-upper, alpha-lower) or a Numbering object applies to every list level; an array gives one entry per level (index = level, the last entry repeats for deeper levels). Counting follows PowerPoint: consecutive entries of one level count up from its start, and an entry of a shallower level restarts the deeper levels. Absent = bullets. Valid only with `items` or `bullets`. Native PowerPoint export writes a:buAutoNum with the matching scheme and startAt; the preview draws the same numbers at the same marker geometry.

fields.name: image
fields.description: Shorthand for one image block: the picture composes as body content, like { type: 'image', image: value }, with the effective design.imageFit. A v2 layout binds it to a compatible body region; a region's bleed setting may extend its outer edges to the slide edge. For fit, focus, treatments or an explicit placement use an image block in blocks; for a full-slide picture behind the content use design.background. Presence of this field infers type 'image'.

fields.name: video
fields.description: Full-slide video source. Presence of this field infers type 'video'. Engines do not play video: the preview draws a placeholder (a play badge with the asset's title or source as its caption), and PPTX export draws the same placeholder as native shapes linked to an http(s) source, with no embedded media. Native playback is out of scope (docs/programs/release-readiness).

fields.name: chart
fields.description: Full-slide chart payload. Presence of this field infers type 'chart'.

fields.name: table
fields.description: Full-slide table payload. Presence of this field infers type 'table'.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Full-slide code payload. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries optional syntax language and filename metadata.

fields.name: metric
fields.description: Full-slide metric payload. A string or number is shorthand for { "value": value }; object form carries optional label, description, unit, delta, trend, and sentiment metadata. Numeric values remain numbers; renderers format them for display. Presence of this field infers type 'metric'.

fields.name: quote
fields.description: Full-slide quote payload. A string is shorthand for { "text": value }; object form carries optional attribution and source metadata. Presence of this field infers type 'quote'.

fields.name: timeline
fields.description: Full-slide timeline payload. An array is shorthand for { "events": value }; object form carries optional name and description metadata. Presence of this field infers type 'timeline'.

fields.name: diagram
fields.description: Full-slide diagram payload: Mermaid, Graphviz DOT or PlantUML source drawn in the deck's fonts and colors. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries the source syntax and a text alternative. Presence of this field infers type 'diagram'.

fields.name: caption
fields.description: Caption for the slide's root image, chart, table, video or diagram payload. Valid only when the slide root holds exactly one of those payloads.

fields.name: blocks
fields.description: Layout-agnostic content blocks rendered together as a composed payload when exact placement is unspecified. At slide root, multiple content payload kinds with no explicit type, blocks, or regions are accepted as shorthand for equivalent blocks.

fields.name: shapes
fields.description: Shapes and connectors drawn over the composed slide, above its content and furniture, in array order (later entries on top). They never move content. An entry with connector is a connector between two blocks or overlay shapes; any other entry is an overlay shape placed by x, y, width and height (fractions of the slide) or at (against a block). See docs/shapes.md.

fields.name: design
fields.description: Slide-level design applied on top of the deck-wide design.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Speaker notes shown in presenter view.

fields.name: section
fields.description: PowerPoint-style slide section label. Consecutive slides with the same value belong to the same section in presenter view, outlines, and PowerPoint section-aware exports. Also the slide-scoped built-in variable '{{slide.section}}', for example in a header text.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Whether the slide is hidden from the presented sequence. The player skips it, the PPTX export writes it as a hidden slide, and per-slide image and PDF output skips it unless the caller asks to include hidden slides (opf CLI: --include-hidden; the deck-level toSvg: the opt-in skipHidden). A slide named explicitly (opf convert --slides, toSvg with a slide number) is still rendered.

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows at slide scope; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips. Use for review state, generation provenance, or authoring conventions such as { "authoring": { "locked": true } }.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Optional stable identifier for this payload, unique among slide and payload ids in the document. Use when another system needs to address the payload across edits — patch-style agent edits, comments, review state, or generation provenance. Identity survives reordering where array indexes do not.

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows at payload scope; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Pin a root block (slides.N.blocks.I) to a region of the slide's template layout by name. The block goes to that region when the region exists, accepts the block's kind and has room; otherwise the pin is ignored with a warning (opf/region-unknown, opf/region-kind or opf/region-full) and the block is placed by its kind. Blocks without a pin are bound by reading order, role and kind. A pin on a nested block, or on a slide without a template layout, has no effect.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Optional content kind. When omitted, engines infer the kind from the fields present: a block with 'shape' and no 'image', or with 'path', is a shape block.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text payload. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Structured list payload (type 'list'). Each item is either a plain string, a TextRun[] rich text sequence, or a ListItem object with optional `description`. List nesting uses item.level rather than nested content payloads. Use `items` when entries share a shape or any entry needs a `description`; use `bullets` for plain talking points. Both draw the same marker, nesting and numbering. A block or region holds `items` or `bullets`, never both, and `items` cannot sit beside `text`.

fields.name: bullets
fields.description: Prose bullet payload: short talking points, each standing alone. Presence of this field infers type 'text', so it may sit beside `text` in one payload. Entries have no `description`; use `items` for entries with supporting detail.

fields.name: numbering
fields.description: Number the payload's `items` or `bullets` instead of bulleting them. A style name (arabic, roman-upper, roman-lower, alpha-upper, alpha-lower) or a Numbering object applies to every list level; an array gives one entry per level (index = level, the last entry repeats for deeper levels). Counting follows PowerPoint: consecutive entries of one level count up from its start, and an entry of a shallower level restarts the deeper levels. Absent = bullets. Valid only with `items` or `bullets`. Native PowerPoint export writes a:buAutoNum with the matching scheme and startAt; the preview draws the same numbers at the same marker geometry.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Lay the payload's `items` or `bullets` out in columns. 'auto' tries 1, 2 then 3 equal columns at the starting text size and uses the first count at which the list fits, as long as a column stays at least a quarter of the slide wide; when none fits, 'auto' takes the count (1, 2 or 3) whose fitted size is largest, preferring fewer columns on a tie, and sets the list in one column only when its lines stay within the prose measure (or it is a type-scale step larger). A list of 6 or fewer entries is never split by 'auto'; it shrinks in one column. 1, 2 or 3 fixes the count. Column breaks fall between items (a nested item stays with its parent) and keep the columns as even as possible; numbering continues and reading order runs column by column. A lone list in a layout region with listColumns: 'auto' behaves as 'auto'.

fields.name: image
fields.description: Source for an image item.

fields.name: fit
fields.description: Image payloads only. How the picture fills its frame: 'cover' fills it and crops what overflows around focus; 'contain' shows the whole picture, in a frame of its own proportions placed at the region's anchor (top by default); 'stretch' scales it to the frame exactly; 'auto' covers when the crop keeps at least 85% of the picture's width or height and contains otherwise (an SVG, or a picture whose size cannot be read from the document, is contained), so a photo close to its frame's shape fills it and any other is shown whole. Default: the effective design.imageFit, else 'cover' in a layout and 'contain' on a slide with no layout.

fields.name: focus
fields.description: Image payloads only. Point of the picture to keep in view when 'cover' crops it. Ignored by the other fits. Without a focus a portrait picture (taller than wide) cropped into a wider frame keeps y 0.3 so heads stay in frame; every other crop is centered.

fields.name: aspectRatio
fields.description: Image payloads only. Width-to-height ratio of the frame: the frame becomes the largest centered box with this ratio inside the block's region, for example 2.39 for a cinematic letterbox or 0.5 for a phone-shaped frame. shape 'circle' always uses 1.

fields.name: shape
fields.description: The preset geometry. Without 'image' it makes the block a shape block: the preset drawn at the block's own fitted size with 'fill', 'stroke' and 'style', and 'text' inside its text rectangle. On an image block it is the frame's mask, exported as the picture's native preset geometry (a:prstGeom); 0.33 renamed rectangle, rounded and circle to rect, roundRect and ellipse, and every other preset is a mask too. 'ellipse' makes an image frame square. Default rect.

fields.name: stroke
fields.description: Shape and image blocks. The line along the outline: a shape's outline or the picture frame's shape (renamed from the picture key 'border' in 0.33, no alias). Without it a shape takes its style's line; a picture has none.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Custom geometry instead of a preset (a:custGeom): SVG path data in a 0 to 1 box, or { d, viewBox }. A block with 'path' is a shape block.

fields.name: fill
fields.description: Shape blocks only. 'none', a ColorRef, { gradient } or { pattern }. Default the style's fill.

fields.name: style
fields.description: Shape blocks only. The theme shape style, as PowerPoint's shape styles (p:style with a:lnRef, a:fillRef, a:effectRef and a:fontRef): subtle is a light tint of accent1 with an accent1 line and dark text, moderate (the default) a solid accent1 fill with a darker line and light text, intense accent1 25% darker with no line, light bold text and the soft shadow. none draws nothing the author did not set. An explicit fill, stroke or effect wins over the style's.

fields.name: rotate
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Rotation in degrees, clockwise, about the shape's center (a:xfrm rot). Composition keeps the unrotated box; the rotated outline may reach past it.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Mirror the geometry (a:xfrm flipH, flipV). The text is not mirrored.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Vertical placement of the text in the text rectangle (a:bodyPr anchor t, ctr, b). Default middle.

fields.name: padding
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Text insets inside the text rectangle.

fields.name: textDirection
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Text direction (a:bodyPr vert horz, vert, vert270, wordArtVert): vertical turns the text 90 degrees clockwise, vertical270 270, stacked stacks the letters top to bottom. Default horizontal.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Alternative text for screen readers (p:cNvPr descr). Without it a shape's text is what is read.

fields.name: decorative
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Mark the shape decorative (a16:decorative): screen readers skip it and the accessibility checker does not ask for alt text.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Keep the shape in the file but do not draw it (p:cNvPr hidden). Composition still gives it its room. A link on a hidden shape cannot be clicked and is a validation finding (opf/shape-link-hidden).

fields.name: link
fields.description: Shape blocks only. URL opened when the shape is clicked in a slide show (a:hlinkClick): an http(s) URL, a 'mailto:' address or a 'tel:' number.

fields.name: shadow
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Outer shadow.

fields.name: innerShadow
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Inner shadow.

fields.name: glow
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Glow.

fields.name: softEdge
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Soft edges (a:softEdge): the radius over which the outline fades, in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: reflection
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Reflection.

fields.name: blur
fields.description: Shape blocks only. Blur of the whole shape (a:blur), radius in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge.

fields.name: adjust
fields.description: Shape and image blocks. The preset's adjust handles (a:avLst), named as DrawingML's guides (adj, adj1, adj2 ... and hexagon's vf): fractions of the shape's shorter side or of its size as the preset defines them, degrees for an angle, never DrawingML's 100000ths or 60000ths. roundRect's adj is the corner radius as a fraction of the shorter side (0.16667 by default, 0 to 0.5). An unknown name or a value out of the preset's range is a validation finding (opf/shape-adjust-unknown, opf/shape-adjust-range) and the preset's default is drawn.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Image and shape blocks. On an image: the picture's opacity, exported as a native alphaModFix; the stroke and overlay keep their own. On a shape: the fill's opacity (a:alpha on the fill color, multiplied with an eight-digit hex alpha); the stroke and text keep theirs. Default 1.

fields.name: recolor
fields.description: Image payloads only. Grayscale or duotone treatment of the picture's pixels.

fields.name: overlay
fields.description: Image payloads only. Scrim over the picture in the frame's shape, or a band along one edge of a rectangle frame.

fields.name: placement
fields.description: Image payloads only, and only on a top-level block (slides.N.blocks.I), at most one per edge. Bleeds the image to one slide edge; the headings and the other blocks compose in the rest of the slide.

fields.name: portrait
fields.description: Image payloads only: how a person's picture is drawn in a team. A person is a group of a picture followed by a name (a list of one entry, whose description holds the role and a line, or a short text); a slide whose body is only people is a team. 'top' draws each picture across the top of its card at the card's width, 'side' beside the text at 40% of the card's width (on the logical start side), 'avatar' as the small picture over the name. Without it the engine chooses: 'top' for 2 to 4 people, 'side' for 5 or 6, the avatar for more or when a card is too narrow. The first person's value applies to the whole team, so the cards stay equal. A 'top' or 'side' picture covers its frame around `focus` (the upper third when none is given) in a rounded frame unless `shape` says otherwise; names, roles and lines keep their size, and a frame flatter than 4:3 falls back to the avatar. Ignored on a picture that is not a person's.

fields.name: video
fields.description: Source for a video item. Engines do not play video: the preview draws a placeholder (a play badge with the asset's title or source as its caption), and PPTX export draws the same placeholder as native shapes linked to an http(s) source, with no embedded media. Native playback is out of scope (docs/programs/release-readiness).

fields.name: chart
fields.description: Chart payload. Presence of this field infers type 'chart'.

fields.name: table
fields.description: Table payload. Presence of this field infers type 'table'.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Code payload. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries optional syntax language and filename metadata.

fields.name: metric
fields.description: Metric payload. A string or number is shorthand for { "value": value }; object form carries optional label, description, unit, delta, trend, and sentiment metadata. Numeric values remain numbers; renderers format them for display.

fields.name: quote
fields.description: Quote payload. A string is shorthand for { "text": value }; object form carries optional attribution, role, photo and source metadata.

fields.name: timeline
fields.description: Timeline payload ordered by narrative or chronology.

fields.name: diagram
fields.description: Diagram payload: Mermaid source (flowchart, sequence, state, class, ER, mindmap, timeline, journey, C4, architecture and the other built-in Mermaid families), or Graphviz DOT or PlantUML source with 'syntax', drawn in the deck's fonts and colors. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries the source syntax and a text alternative. Presence of this field infers type 'diagram'.

fields.name: caption
fields.description: Caption for an image, chart, table, video or diagram payload, composed inside the block's region (below the media by default). Invalid on other payload kinds and on groups.

fields.name: blocks
fields.description: Ordered children of a group. Each child is a leaf or another group.

fields.name: composition
fields.description: Arrangement within this group. Only minFontSize, maxFontSize and overflow inherit from the parent; strict overflow cannot be weakened.

fields.name: emphasis
fields.description: true draws this block or group on the slide's emphasis surface: a contrasting card in its cell (a dark card on a light slide, an accent card on a dark one), from the deck's own scheme slots, with every text color on it at 4.5:1 or more against its fill. A slide has one emphasis surface: the first block or group with emphasis: true in reading order takes it, and any other is drawn without it (composition diagnostic emphasis-ignored). Without any, a slide's short last text block (60 characters or fewer) after longer blocks is drawn as a band at the foot of the body, and one of 30 or fewer after a lone long text as a pill right under that text; neither is drawn where it would cost another block its fitted size. Without any either, the second card of a before-and-after or problem-and-solution pair, or the one tier of a set marked recommended or most popular, takes the surface and the other cards of the pair or set are drawn on plain cards (read from the blocks' labels and short texts, never from ids). false keeps a block out of those automatic rules.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: Groups only: an icon drawn on a chip at the top of the group, before its heading, as a card of features or topics draws one: "<set>:<name>" ("lucide:shield-check"), a name from the deck's icons, or an SVG source. A list entry and a metric take their own `icon`. Decoration only: when the slide has no room for it without setting text smaller, it is not drawn (finding opf/icon-dropped). See docs/icons.md.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Quoted text: a string, or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored phrase, bold, a link, or a citation or footnote marker). The engine draws the surrounding quotation marks.

fields.name: attribution
fields.description: Person or organization credited for the quote. Drawn after the quote text, in the muted text color.

fields.name: role
fields.description: Title and organization of the attributed person. Drawn on its own line under the attribution; without an attribution it stands alone. It does not replace the attribution, so the person's name belongs in 'attribution'.

fields.name: photo
fields.description: Headshot of the attributed person, drawn as a circle beside the attribution and role lines (on the logical start side: left in a left-to-right deck, right in a right-to-left deck), or as a tall portrait beside the quote (see `portrait`). Give it alt text (validate's opf/missing-alt-text rule checks it). A raster photograph works best; an SVG exports as its PNG raster because the mask is not confirmed on SVG pictures in PowerPoint. An unresolved source draws the ordinary image placeholder.

fields.name: portrait
fields.description: How the `photo` is drawn. 'side' draws it as a tall picture at the start of the quote (about a quarter of its width, rounded, cropped around the upper third), the quote text beside it and centered against it; 'avatar' as the circle beside the attribution. Without it the engine draws 'side' when the quote is at least 640 px wide and every part of the quote keeps the size it has beside the avatar (the picture takes a narrower share where the text needs the room), and the avatar otherwise (several quotes side by side, a quote beside other blocks). Needs `photo`.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Optional quote source, citation, or URL. Follows the attribution and role after ' - '.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Source code text to display.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Language identifier used for syntax highlighting.

fields.name: filename
fields.description: Optional file label shown with the code block.

fields.name: highlight
fields.description: Source lines to emphasize, 1-based: each entry is a line number or an inclusive [start, end] range, so [3, [5, 7]] marks lines 3 and 5 to 7. Lines are counted by line break in 'source', so a line that wraps stays one line. Engines draw a theme-derived band behind the marked lines and dim the other lines slightly, keeping every line at least 4.5:1 against its background; PPTX export draws one native rectangle behind the line text boxes and import restores the list. A line number past the last line, or a range written end before start, gets a validation warning (code-highlight-out-of-range, code-highlight-range-reversed) and is ignored. When a code block is paginated across slides each page keeps the lines that fall on it, renumbered from 1.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Primary metric value.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Metric label.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional supporting context for the metric.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: Metric unit, suffix, or currency marker.

fields.name: delta
fields.description: Metric change value.

fields.name: trend
fields.description: Metric trend direction. The preview and the PowerPoint export draw it as an arrow that always points the way the trend does (up, down or flat), before the delta on its line (or before the label without a delta), and color the arrow and the delta text by `sentiment`. The word itself is not drawn; it is the arrow's text alternative.

fields.name: sentiment
fields.description: Whether the change is good news. Positive draws the trend arrow and the trend and delta text in green, negative in red and neutral in the neutral text colour, each kept at 4.5:1 contrast or more against the slide background. When absent the colour follows the trend: up is positive, down is negative and flat is neutral. Set it when the direction is not the verdict, for example positive on a falling churn, cost or latency trend. The arrow always keeps the direction of `trend`. Only the trend arrow and the trend and delta text take the colour, so sentiment has no visible effect on a metric without a trend.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: An icon drawn on a chip above the metric: "<set>:<name>" ("lucide:users"), a name from the deck's icons, or an SVG source. Decoration only: when the slide has no room for it without setting text smaller, it is not drawn (finding opf/icon-dropped). See docs/icons.md.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The diagram source. With syntax 'mermaid' (the default) it is Mermaid 12.1 text whose first line names the diagram type (flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, erDiagram, gantt, pie, mindmap, timeline, journey, quadrantChart, xychart, sankey, gitGraph, C4Context, block, architecture-beta, kanban, packet, radar-beta, treemap, venn-beta, ishikawa, requirementDiagram and the other built-in families; ZenUML is not supported). Mermaid themes, colors in themeVariables and click callbacks are ignored: the deck's design decides the colors and fonts. With syntax 'dot' it is one Graphviz DOT graph (graph or digraph), laid out in layers as Graphviz's dot engine does: rankdir, node shapes, edge styles, arrowheads, labels and subgraph cluster_* groups are drawn; colors, fonts, sizes and positions are the deck's; a graph whose layout attribute names another engine (neato, fdp, sfdp, circo, twopi, osage, patchwork) is not drawn. With syntax 'plantuml' it is one PlantUML diagram from @startuml (or @startmindmap, @startgantt) to its @end line: sequence, class, state, activity (the current syntax), use case, component and deployment diagrams, mind maps and gantt charts are drawn as the Mermaid family of the same kind; other PlantUML diagrams, the legacy activity syntax and the preprocessor are not drawn, and skinparam, themes and colors are ignored.

fields.name: syntax
fields.description: The language of 'source': 'mermaid' (Mermaid 12.1, the default), 'dot' (Graphviz DOT, drawn with the layered layout) or 'plantuml' (PlantUML, drawn as the Mermaid family of the same kind). OPF reads all three itself; no Graphviz or PlantUML code runs.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Text alternative that says what the diagram shows. Exported as the description of the native shape group or picture. Without it, engines derive one from the diagram's labels.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Short timeline label.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional timeline-level context.

fields.name: events
fields.description: Timeline events ordered by narrative, sequence, or chronology.

fields.name: when
fields.description: Event time, date, or sequence label. Use ISO-like values when possible, but human labels are allowed for quarters, eras, and relative milestones.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Relative length of this consecutive event period. Use the same unit for every event (for example 1 for Week 1 and 4 for Weeks 2–5). Omitted means one unit. When any event supplies duration, both engines draw proportional ranges. The 'when' field stays the authored display label and is never parsed to guess a duration.

fields.name: what
fields.description: Short event label.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional event detail.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Progress of the event, drawn from the deck's own colors by both the SVG renderer and the PPTX exporter. Absent means no status and the event is drawn as a plain filled marker with normal text, which is also how 'done' looks. 'done' is a filled marker in the primary color with normal text. 'current' marks 'we are here': the filled marker is surrounded by a ring and the event label (`what`) is bold. 'planned' is an outlined, hollow marker (primary-color outline over the slide background) with muted secondary text. Text colors keep a 4.5:1 contrast against the slide background. In PPTX the markers are native ellipses (the ring is a second ellipse), and PPTX import restores the status the export recorded. Status describes progress only; schedule health such as at risk or blocked belongs in the event text.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text for the list item. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional supporting detail for the list item. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Zero-based nesting level for the list item.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: An icon drawn on a chip at the start of the entry, in place of its bullet: "<set>:<name>" ("lucide:truck"), a name from the deck's icons, or an SVG source. Drawn on first-level entries of an unnumbered list. Decoration only: when the slide has no room for the chips without setting text smaller, they are not drawn (finding opf/icon-dropped). See docs/icons.md.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Restart the list's numbering at this number for this item (counted at its level); the entries after it continue from it. Only meaningful when the payload has `numbering`. Paginated continuation pages use it to keep the numbers of the whole list.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text for the bullet. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Zero-based nesting level for the bullet.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Restart the list's numbering at this number for this bullet (counted at its level); the entries after it continue from it. Only meaningful when the payload has `numbering`. Paginated continuation pages use it to keep the numbers of the whole list.

fields.name: style
fields.description: Number style. Default arabic.

fields.name: start
fields.description: First number counted at this level. Default 1. Native PowerPoint accepts 1 to 32767.

fields.name: suffix
fields.description: Text after the number: period (1.), paren (1)) or paren-both ((1)). Default period.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Text for this run.

fields.name: bold
fields.description: Whether the run is rendered in bold.

fields.name: italic
fields.description: Whether the run is rendered in italic.

fields.name: underline
fields.description: Whether the run is underlined.

fields.name: strikethrough
fields.description: Whether the run is rendered with a strikethrough line.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Run text color. Documented forms: a hex string ('#RGB', '#RRGGBB', '#RRGGBBAA'), a color-scheme slot or role name resolved through the effective color scheme ('accent2', 'text'), or a 'var:<id>' reference into the top-level variables map. Prefer names over hex so runs survive re-theming. Or the lighter or darker object form of a ColorRef ({ "color": "accent1", "darken": 0.25 }). Any other string stays schema-valid so imported decks keep validating: validators warn and renderers fall back to the theme text color.

fields.name: fontSize
fields.description: Run font size in points, the unit presenters know from PowerPoint. It is the one size in OPF that is not in reference pixels: 1 point is 4/3 reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge, so a run of 12 points is as tall as text of 16 reference pixels (composition.minFontSize: 16).

fields.name: fontFamily
fields.description: Run font family override. It wins over the code font a run with 'code' takes.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Whether the run is an inline code span: it is drawn in the design's code font (design.fontScheme.code, else the resolved font scheme's code family, else Roboto Mono), unless the run names its own fontFamily. Only the font changes; there is no background, because a PPTX run cannot have one. Markdown backticks read and write code runs.

fields.name: language
fields.description: BCP-47 language tag of the run, such as 'fr-FR' or 'ja-JP', when it differs from the deck language. It sets the proofing language (PPTX a:rPr lang) and the language the run's script fonts and glyph variants follow (for example the Japanese or the Simplified Chinese face for Han characters); without it the run follows the deck language.

fields.name: link
fields.description: URL to link the run text to: an http(s) URL, a 'mailto:' address or a 'tel:' number, without whitespace. The preview draws it as a link and PPTX export writes a native hyperlink for all three; any other scheme is not valid.

fields.name: superscript
fields.description: Whether the run is rendered as superscript.

fields.name: subscript
fields.description: Whether the run is rendered as subscript.

fields.name: cite
fields.description: One or more ids from the top-level references list that this run cites. Engines draw a superscript marker ('1', or '1,2' for several ids) directly after the run and list '<n> <reference text>' in the slide's footnote area; markers are numbered per deck in order of first use, and the same id keeps its number. An id missing from references is a validation error (cite-unknown-reference). Supported in text, bullets and list item runs, in the slide title, subtitle and tag, and in the quote text.

fields.name: footnote
fields.description: An inline note for this run, without a references entry. Engines draw a superscript marker after the run and list the note in the slide's footnote area; every footnote takes a new number in the deck's marker sequence. Supported in text, bullets and list item runs, in the slide title, subtitle and tag, and in the quote text.

fields.name: text
fields.description: Caption text: a string or TextRun[] for inline rich text.

fields.name: position
fields.description: Where the caption band sits inside the block's region: below the media (default) or above it. Core composition reserves the band and shrinks the media by its height.

fields.name: align
fields.description: Horizontal alignment of the caption text within the block. Defaults to start. Logical: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on (the left for left-to-right text, the right for right-to-left text) and 'end' is the opposite edge.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Identifier runs cite. Unique within the references list.

fields.name: text
fields.description: The reference as it is listed: a string or TextRun[] for inline rich text.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Optional link for the reference; a references slide links its entry to it.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Line color: any ColorRef (eight-digit hex keeps its alpha).

fields.name: width
fields.description: Line width in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge. 0 draws no line, the same as 'none'.

fields.name: dash
fields.description: Dash pattern, by the names Stroke.dash uses.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value in the units of its axis. With a column format of 0%, 0.25 means 25% and 25 means 2500%. On a stacked chart the axis is the stack total. Every reference expands automatic axis bounds when needed.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: Secondary requires a combo chart with an actual secondary line series.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Optional nonblank plain text, shown verbatim. Omission draws no label.

fields.name: labelPosition
fields.description: Logical endpoint. Horizontal start/end mirror in RTL; on bars they mean top/bottom. Requires label.

fields.name: stroke
fields.description: The line's color, width and dash, or 'none' to draw only the label. Defaults: the chart-text neutral, 4/3 reference pixels (1 point) and 'dash'. The value expands the axis bounds whether or not the line is drawn.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Chart type, an engine vocabulary validated directly (no catalog lookup): the chart types OPF supports natively in its preview and PPTX export, plus 'combo' (clustered columns with line series, see 'line' and 'secondaryAxis'). Each engine maps a type to its own chart model; labels and picker groups are catalog display metadata.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Chart data. Inline data uses a tabular columns/rows shape; renderers convert rows to chart series internally. A DatasetRef ({ "dataset": "<id>" }) plots a top-level dataset instead. Data from a spreadsheet or file is imported into inline columns and rows, and its origin is recorded in data.source.

fields.name: mapping
fields.description: Optional series mapping by column name: which column is the category, which is the X column of a scatter chart, and which columns are plotted, in order. Absent keeps the positional rule (first column the category, then the X column for scatter, every other column a series).

fields.name: line
fields.description: Combo charts only (type 'combo'): the plotted series, by column name, that are drawn as lines with markers; every other plotted series is drawn as clustered columns. Absent: the last plotted series is the line. A combo chart keeps at least one column series, so a list that names every series draws the first one as columns. Column series are drawn, exported and listed in the legend first, then the line series on the primary axis, then those on the secondary axis, each in plotted order. A name that is not a column is a 'chart-mapping-unknown-column' error; a column that is not plotted is a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning. On any other chart type it is ignored with a 'chart-option-adapted' warning.

fields.name: secondaryAxis
fields.description: Combo charts only: line series, by column name, plotted against a secondary value axis at the end of the plot (the right; the left in a right-to-left deck, where the category axis runs from the right). That axis has its own scale, and its tick labels use the number format of the first secondary series' column (DataColumn.format), for example '0%' for a margin. Absent: every series shares the primary value axis at the start of the plot (the left; the right in a right-to-left deck). A name that is not a line series (see 'line') stays on the primary axis with a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning; an unknown column is a 'chart-mapping-unknown-column' error. On any other chart type it is ignored with a 'chart-option-adapted' warning.

fields.name: referenceLines
fields.description: Explicit numeric references on the chart's value axis. Supported on the chart types with one value axis for every series: column, bar, line, line-with-markers and area, their stacked forms (stacked-column, stacked-bar, stacked-line, stacked-line-with-markers, stacked-area) and combo. A non-empty list on any other type is the error opf/chart-reference-unsupported-type, so a reference is never dropped silently. Absent or [] means none. Authored order, duplicates and values equal to data are preserved. A vertical chart with two or more categories draws each line from the first category's center to the last's; a bar chart and a chart of one category draw it across the plot. The slide's title and other texts never create, remove or move a reference, and a reference never changes which marks a chart emphasizes.

fields.name: axisTitles
fields.description: Optional axis titles. Absent keeps today's untitled axes. Supported on the chart types that have a category/value (or X/Y) axis pair (column, bar, line, area, scatter, and the histogram, pareto, waterfall and box-and-whisker constructs; the funnel construct takes a category title only; a combo chart also takes 'secondary' when it plots a series on the secondary axis); a title on a type without that axis (pie, doughnut, radar, treemap, world) is dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic by renderers and exporters.

fields.name: legend
fields.description: Optional legend position. 'none' hides the legend. Absent leaves it to the engines: a line chart of two to four series names its series at the line ends and a pie or one-series doughnut names its slices, with no legend; a column, bar, area or combo chart of two to four series shows its legend in the header row above the plot; other multi-series charts and pie and doughnut charts take a legend at the physical right; a single-series chart takes none. A named position shows the legend there even for a single-series chart; 'left' and 'right' are physical sides in every language. Of the Office 2016 constructs only box-and-whisker takes a legend; histogram, pareto, waterfall, funnel, treemap and world drop the option with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

fields.name: dataLabels
fields.description: Optional data labels. true shows value labels at each type's default position and false shows none. Absent leaves it to the engines: no labels, except on a small chart, which labels its values in place of its value axis, the direct labels of line, pie and doughnut charts, and the labels the funnel and treemap constructs draw by default. Use the object form for the label content, position and separator.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Text alternative for the chart: what the data shows (the point and the key numbers), not 'a chart' or 'bar chart'. The preview exposes it as the chart's accessible name (role img with aria-label) and the PowerPoint export writes it as the chart frame's alternative text (descr); import reads it back. An empty string marks the chart decorative, with the same meaning as an empty Asset alt, but it is a reviewed choice that opf/chart-text-alternative still reports as info (a chart almost always carries a message). When absent, validate accepts text beside the chart instead.

fields.name: colors
fields.description: Optional series colors, by position: entry i replaces palette color i, the color of series i (the i-th plotted value column), of slice or category i on a pie, doughnut, treemap or funnel chart, and of the i-th color a histogram, pareto, waterfall or box-and-whisker chart draws with. An entry is any ColorRef: a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role ('accent3', 'secondary') or a 'var:<id>' color variable; a scheme name keeps following the deck if its scheme changes, and is written to PowerPoint as a theme color. Positions past the last entry keep the deck palette (accent1 to accent6, then their tints). A color is kept at 3:1 contrast against the chart panel (a lighter or darker shade is used when it falls short) and 'chart.highlight' wins over it: highlighted marks take the primary color and the rest the muted neutral. A color that cannot be resolved falls back to the palette color for its position. Absent keeps the deck palette exactly.

fields.name: highlight
fields.description: Optional emphasis: the series and/or categories that carry the message. The engines draw the highlighted marks in the deck's primary (accent) color and every other mark in a muted neutral derived from the theme (a light grey on a light chart panel, a dim grey on a dark one); there is no color field. A mark is highlighted when its series OR its category is named. Absent keeps today's colors exactly. Supported on column, bar and line charts (series and categories; on a line a category highlight marks that category's points), pie and doughnut charts (categories, one per slice), and area, scatter and radar charts (series); the histogram, pareto, waterfall, funnel, treemap, box-and-whisker, world and combo constructs drop the option with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic, as does a part the type cannot highlight. A name that matches no column or row label is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Title of the category (X) axis.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Title of the value (Y) axis. On a combo chart, the primary value axis (at the start of the plot).

fields.name: secondary
fields.description: Combo charts only: title of the secondary value axis at the end of the plot (the right; the left in a right-to-left deck), drawn rotated like the primary value axis title. Dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic on any other chart type and on a combo chart without 'secondaryAxis'.

fields.name: series
fields.description: Series (value columns) to highlight: all marks of each named series. A name that is not a column is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error; a column that is not plotted as a series (the category or X column, or one mapping.series leaves out) highlights nothing and is a 'chart-highlight-adapted' warning.

fields.name: categories
fields.description: Categories (row labels) to highlight: the marks of each named category (a column or bar of every series, a line's points, a pie or doughnut slice). A label no row has is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error.

fields.name: content
fields.description: Which parts a label shows. Defaults to ['value']. 'percent' is the share of the total and exists only on pie and doughnut charts; 'category' shows the category name (the X value on a scatter chart). A part a chart type cannot show is dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

fields.name: position
fields.description: Where a label sits relative to its mark. 'auto' (the default) is the type's default: outside-end for clustered columns and bars, pie slices and the histogram, pareto and waterfall constructs; center for stacked columns and bars; above for line and scatter points. Clustered columns and bars and the histogram, pareto and waterfall constructs take center, inside-end, inside-base and outside-end; stacked columns and bars take center, inside-end and inside-base; pie takes center, inside-end and outside-end; line and scatter points take above, below, left, right and center. Area, doughnut and radar charts and the funnel and treemap constructs take only 'auto' (the box-and-whisker and world constructs have no data labels). A combo chart places the labels of its column series like clustered columns and those of its line series like line points; a position only one part takes applies to that part, and the other part keeps its default (outside-end, above). An unsupported position falls back to 'auto' with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

fields.name: separator
fields.description: Text between the parts of a label that shows more than one. Defaults to ', '.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Optional column labels. Labels may be strings, rich runs, styled cell objects or DataColumn objects ({ "name", "format" }). A header's 'format' (DataColumn or StyledTableCell) is the column's number format; a body cell's own format wins. Null is an empty label or a placeholder covered by a preceding column span.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Two-dimensional table row data; each row aligns by index with columns when columns are supplied.

fields.name: dataset
fields.description: Id of a top-level dataset that supplies this table's headers, rows and column formats. Excludes 'rows' and 'columns'. An unknown id is a 'dataset-unknown' error.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Dataset tables only: the dataset columns to show, by name and in order. Absent shows every column. An unknown name is a 'dataset-field-unknown' error.

fields.name: alt
fields.description: Text alternative for the table: what it shows (the point and the key numbers), not 'a table'. The preview exposes it as the table's accessible name (role group with aria-label; the cells stay readable) and the PowerPoint export writes it as the table frame's alternative text (descr); import reads it back. An empty string hides a purely decorative table, with the same meaning as an empty Asset alt. The alt is a summary read before the cells, which stay readable, so it is most useful for a large or dense table; validate does not require one and does not report a missing one.

fields.name: highlight
fields.description: Optional emphasis: the body rows that carry the message, named by their first-column (key) text exactly as 'chart.highlight' names categories, as text; a key shared by several rows highlights each of them. The engines draw a highlighted row on an accent tint of the table surface (15% of the deck's primary color, mixed less where the cell text would fall under 4.5:1); a cell with its own 'style.fill' keeps it. Absent, the engines highlight the rows the slide's other texts name (its title, a sentence, a list entry, a quote or a chart's alt) when they agree on some rows but not all; an empty 'rows' list turns that off. PPTX export writes the tint as each cell's fill and import restores the list. A name no row has is a 'table-highlight-unknown-name' error.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Key texts (the first cell of each body row, as text) of the rows to highlight.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Ordered column labels for the chart data table. A label is a string or a DataColumn ({ "name", "format" }) whose number format the data labels, value axis and exported workbook use.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Tabular chart rows. Each row aligns by index with columns.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Optional provenance: where this inline data came from. Engines never read, fetch or refresh it; they keep it through editing, export and re-import.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Column label, used as the series name, the table header and the name 'fields' and 'chart.mapping' address.

fields.name: format
fields.description: Number format of the column's number values (data labels, value axis, table cells, exported workbook). Absent: the General form.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Where the data came from: an 'asset:<id>' reference, a URL, or a relative or local path.

fields.name: sheet
fields.description: Sheet or table name inside a spreadsheet source.

fields.name: range
fields.description: A1-style range inside a spreadsheet source.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: The source fields the data was taken from, in order.

fields.name: retrieved
fields.description: When the data was taken from the source: an ISO 8601 date or date-time.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free-form note about the source.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human name of the dataset, shown by editors.

fields.name: description
fields.description: What the dataset holds.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Ordered, uniquely named columns.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: Rows of scalar cells (string, number, boolean, null); each row aligns by index with columns.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Optional provenance. Engines never read, fetch or refresh it.

fields.name: dataset
fields.description: Id of the dataset. An unknown id is a 'dataset-unknown' error.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: The dataset columns to use, by name and in order. Absent uses every column.

fields.name: category
fields.description: The label (category) column. Default: the first column.

fields.name: x
fields.description: The X column of an XY (scatter) chart. Default: the second column (the first, when the category is the second column), and only when there are three or more columns: with two, the second column is the one series, plotted against row numbers. An X that leaves no series is plotted as the series with a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning.

fields.name: series
fields.description: The plotted columns, in order. Default: every column that is not the category or the X column.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Editable cell content; styling and spans do not change its scalar type or rich runs.

fields.name: colSpan
fields.description: Number of grid columns covered, starting at this cell. Covered positions must contain null. Default 1.

fields.name: rowSpan
fields.description: Number of grid rows covered, starting at this cell. Covered positions must contain null. Header cells cannot span into body rows. Default 1.

fields.name: format
fields.description: Number format. On a body cell it formats that cell's number value (and wins over the column's format); on a header cell (in 'columns') it is the column's format, the same as a DataColumn header. Strings, booleans, null and rich runs display unchanged.

fields.name: fill
fields.description: Cell background: a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference. Eight-digit hex colors include alpha; #00000000 is transparent.

fields.name: color
fields.description: Default text color, overridden by individual rich run colors. Accepts a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference.

fields.name: bold
fields.description: Bold cell text. Runs that set their own bold keep it; a number cell stays bold and still uses the cell's or column's number format.

fields.name: align
fields.description: Horizontal text alignment inside the cell. Logical: 'start' is the edge a paragraph starts on (the left for left-to-right text, the right for right-to-left text) and 'end' is the opposite edge.

fields.name: verticalAlign
fields.description: Vertical alignment inside the padded cell box.

fields.name: borders
fields.description: Independent cell edges. An omitted edge keeps the table's default rule: a line under every row (and over the first row), none between columns. Width 0 removes an edge.

fields.name: default
fields.description: The catalog bare ids come from: its source and the records of it this document embeds. false turns off the catalog fallback for bare ids.

fields.name: custom
fields.description: Records the document defines itself, referenced by bare id. Checked first for every bare id. Forking a catalog record copies it here under a new id, so the change of ownership is visible.

fields.name: layouts
fields.description: Layout records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-layout/v2. Referenced from Slide.layout.

fields.name: themes
fields.description: Theme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-theme/v1. Referenced from design.theme.

fields.name: colorSchemes
fields.description: Colour-scheme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-color-scheme/v1. Referenced from design.colorScheme and a theme's colorScheme.

fields.name: fontSchemes
fields.description: Font-scheme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-font-scheme/v1. Referenced from design.fontScheme, a theme's fontScheme and a language's font schemes.

fields.name: narratives
fields.description: Narrative records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-narrative/v1. Referenced from narrative.

fields.name: audiences
fields.description: Audience records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-audience/v1. Referenced from audience.

fields.name: purposes
fields.description: Purpose records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-purpose/v1. Referenced from purpose.

fields.name: tones
fields.description: Tone records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-tone/v1. Referenced from tone.

fields.name: iconSets
fields.description: Icon-set records keyed by set id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-icon-set/v1, holding only the icons the document uses (no licenseText or tags). Referenced from an icon as "<set>:<name>".

fields.name: mode
fields.description: auto chooses a grid from available space and content; grid uses columns; row and column use one horizontal or vertical track.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: Column count for grid. In auto mode this caps the number of columns.

fields.name: gap
fields.description: Space between cells as a fraction of the container short edge (canvas at slide root). Default 0.03333333333333333.

fields.name: padding
fields.description: Inset as a fraction of the container short edge. Default 0.08 on a slide, 0 inside a group.

fields.name: weights
fields.description: Relative track sizes: columns for row/grid/auto, rows for column. Omitted tracks have weight 1; extra weights are ignored.

fields.name: minFontSize
fields.description: Minimum readable text size in reference pixels at a 720-pixel canvas short edge. Default 16. Overflow is diagnosed when text cannot fit at this size.

fields.name: maxFontSize
fields.description: Largest body text size in reference pixels at a 720-pixel canvas short edge: paragraphs, lists, quotes, metrics and timelines are never set larger, their growth included (headings, tables, code and charts keep their sizes). Never lowers text under minFontSize. paginate writes it on the pages after the first, so the pages of one slide share its type sizes.

fields.name: overflow
fields.description: warn returns diagnostics for content that does not fit; error rejects layout. Content is never silently removed. Default warn.

additionalProperties.description: Handle or URL for the platform identified by the property key.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

caption.description: A slide's caption belongs to its root image, chart, table, video or diagram.

path.description: A custom outline makes a shape block; a picture's mask is a preset 'shape'.

caption.description: A caption belongs to an image, chart, table, video or diagram.

additionalProperties.description: A named catalog: its source and the records of it this document embeds. References name it as a prefix ('acme:hero').
One embedded record: the fields of the kind's companion schema without '$schema' and 'id'.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a purpose record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The purpose's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable purpose name shown in pickers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the purpose — what this deck is trying to accomplish.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing when to use this purpose and how it should shape a deck.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: Desired audience outcome after the presentation.

fields.name: successCriteria
fields.description: Observable signals that the deck accomplished this purpose.

fields.name: recommendedNarratives
fields.description: Soft cross-link: ids of narratives in the same catalog that work well for this purpose. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: recommendedTones
fields.description: Soft cross-link: ids of tones in the same catalog that work well for this purpose. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional.

fields.name: src
fields.description: Main preview image (PNG/JPG).

fields.name: thumbnailSrc
fields.description: Smaller thumbnail preview suited to dense grid views.

fields.name: vectorSrc
fields.description: SVG / vector preview for crisp scaling at any size.

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies this record as a social-platform entry in the openpresentation.org catalog.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The social platform's key, as written in a Socials object. Lowercase kebab-case.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable platform name shown in pickers and footers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the platform — what it's used for and who's on it.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing the platform and any rendering conventions (e.g., handle prefixes, distributed instances).

fields.name: baseUrl
fields.description: Canonical base URL of the platform — used as the prefix when normalizing handles to full URLs.

fields.name: profileUrlPattern
fields.description: URL pattern for individual member profiles. Use '{handle}' as the placeholder for the handle (with the prefix already stripped).

fields.name: companyUrlPattern
fields.description: Optional URL pattern for organization / company pages, when the platform distinguishes them from member profiles. Use '{handle}' as the placeholder.

fields.name: handlePrefix
fields.description: Conventional prefix character displayed before the handle (e.g. '@' for X / Mastodon / Threads / TikTok). Empty string when no prefix is used. Renderers strip it before substituting into URL patterns.

fields.name: handleExample
fields.description: Example handle in its conventional rendered form, used by picker UIs and validation hints.

fields.name: brandColor
fields.description: Brand color (hex) for branded icon chips, link styling, or section accents in authoring UIs. Catalog metadata: engines do not draw it.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional; engines fall back gracefully when previews aren't available.

fields.name: src

fields.name: $schema
fields.description: Identifies a published record file as a theme record. Required in a published file; an embedded copy omits it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The theme's id in its catalog, lowercase kebab-case. Required in a published record file; a document references the record by it (a bare id, or 'name:id' for a named group) and embeds it keyed by it, without this field.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable theme name shown in pickers.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-sentence positioning of the theme — when to reach for it.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer prose describing what the theme looks and feels like and the kinds of decks it suits.

fields.name: colorScheme
fields.description: The theme's default colour scheme: a reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved like design.colorScheme, but in the theme's own catalogs group first.

fields.name: fontScheme
fields.description: The theme's default font scheme: a reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved like design.fontScheme, but in the theme's own catalogs group first.

fields.name: variants
fields.description: The color variants the theme offers (OPF 0.23), for example light, light-alt, dark and dark-alt: named values of design.variant over the theme's one color scheme, so a dark deck is a variant of a theme and not a theme of its own. A picker lists them by name; choosing one sets design.variant (or a slide's design.variant) to the entry's 'variant'. A document stores that value and never the id, so a variant needs no record and the theme does not change when its variants do. The entry ids are unique within a theme.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.description: Default slide size for this theme. Accepts the same preset values as design.dimensions.preset.

fields.name: design
fields.description: The theme's design defaults (OPF 0.19), so a house style such as boxed content or centred titles is set once: the keys and values of the deck's design for titleAlignment, contentAlignment, contentBox, contentDirection, imageFit and listBullet. Per key the slide's design wins, then the deck's design, then this, then the layout record's design, then the engine default.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Visual previews of the record, used by picker UIs and inline rendering. All sub-fields are optional; engines fall back gracefully when previews aren't available.
